Essential (Primary) Hypertension.name: Essential (Primary) Hypertension
Essential (Primary) Hypertension.symptoms: Morning occipital headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, episodic blurred vision, palpitations, mild chest tightness, often asymptomatic with high blood pressure readings above 140/90
symptoms_list: often asymptomatic with high blood pressure readings above 140/90
Essential (Primary) Hypertension.treatment: Lifestyle first (weight loss ≥5%, DASH diet, salt <5 g/day, exercise 150 min/week, limit alcohol, quit smoking). Drugs for Stage 2 (≥140/90) or Stage 1 (130–139/80–89) with high CV risk, diabetes or CKD; target <130/80 (2025 AHA/ACC). Start two-drug single-pill combination if BP ≥20/10 above target.
medications: Telmisartan 40–80 mg OD or Losartan 50–100 mg OD
Chlorthalidone 12.5–25 mg OD or Indapamide 1.5 mg SR OD. Resistant HTN: add Spironolactone 25–50 mg OD.
Essential (Primary) Hypertension.precautions: Do not combine ACEi + ARB. Check K⁺ and creatinine 1–2 weeks after starting ACEi/ARB/spironolactone. ACEi/ARB contraindicated in pregnancy. Avoid NSAIDs. Rise slowly (orthostatic hypotension in elderly).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Essential (Primary) Hypertension symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypertensive Emergency.name: Hypertensive Emergency
Hypertensive Emergency.symptoms: Severe throbbing headache, blood pressure over 180/120 mmHg, sudden blurred vision or vision loss, acute shortness of breath, crushing chest tightness, confusion, nausea, vomiting
symptoms_list: sudden blurred vision or vision loss
Hypertensive Emergency.treatment: BP >180/120 with acute target-organ damage. ICU admission; reduce MAP by no more than 25% in first hour, then to 160/100 over 2–6 h, then normal over 24–48 h (exceptions: aortic dissection SBP <120 within 20 min; ischemic stroke specific targets).
medications: IV Labetalol 20 mg bolus then 20–80 mg q10min (max 300 mg) or infusion 1–2 mg/min
Nicardipine 5 mg/h, titrate 2.5 mg/h q5–15min (max 15 mg/h)
Hypertensive Emergency.precautions: Avoid sublingual nifedipine (precipitous drop → stroke/MI). Avoid beta-blockers alone in cocaine toxicity. Nitroprusside → cyanide toxicity with prolonged use/renal failure.
emergency_flags: Severe headache, chest pain, or vision loss

Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrom.name: Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrome
Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrom.symptoms: Exertional retrosternal chest pressure or squeezing discomfort, chest tightness provoked by walking uphill or emotional stress, pain radiating to left shoulder neck or jaw, relieved within minutes by rest or nitroglycerin
symptoms_list: Exertional retrosternal chest pressure or squeezing discomfort
chest tightness provoked by walking uphill or emotional stress
pain radiating to left shoulder neck or jaw
relieved within minutes by rest or nitroglycerin
Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrom.treatment: Risk-factor control, antianginal therapy, antiplatelet + high-intensity statin; revascularization (PCI/CABG) for refractory symptoms or high-risk anatomy.
medications: Atorvastatin 40–80 mg OD or Rosuvastatin 20–40 mg OD
Metoprolol succinate 25–200 mg OD or Bisoprolol 2.5–10 mg OD
Ezetimibe 10 mg if LDL above target.
Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrom.precautions: No nitrates within 24 h of sildenafil (48 h tadalafil). Avoid non-dihydropyridine CCB with beta-blocker in heart failure/bradycardia. Seek emergency care if rest pain >20 min.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrome symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.name: Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.symptoms: Acute severe crushing substernal chest pain lasting over 20 minutes, radiation to left arm neck and jaw, cold diaphoresis, severe shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, profound sense of impending doom
symptoms_list: Acute severe crushing substernal chest pain lasting over 20 minutes
radiation to left arm neck and jaw
Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.treatment: Emergency reperfusion: primary PCI within 90–120 min of first medical contact; fibrinolysis within 30 min if PCI unavailable within 120 min. Oxygen only if SpO₂ <90%.
medications: Aspirin 162–325 mg chewed then 75–100 mg OD
P2Y12: Ticagrelor 180 mg load then 90 mg BD or Prasugrel 60 mg then 10 mg OD (or Clopidogrel 600 mg load)
Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.precautions: Rule out dissection before anticoagulation/thrombolysis. Avoid nitrates in RV infarct, hypotension, PDE5 use. Prasugrel contraindicated with prior stroke/TIA. Watch arrhythmias and mechanical complications.
emergency_flags: Severe crushing chest pain radiating to left arm or jaw
Acute ST elevation on ECG requiring emergency reperfusion

NSTEMI / Unstable Angina.name: NSTEMI / Unstable Angina
NSTEMI / Unstable Angina.symptoms: Accelerating or crescendo chest tightness occurring at rest or with minimal exertion, prolonged substernal chest pain, shortness of breath, diaphoresis, lightheadedness without obvious ST elevation
symptoms_list: Accelerating or crescendo chest tightness occurring at rest or with minimal exertion
investigations: serial hs-troponin (0/1 h or 0/2 h algorithm)
NSTEMI / Unstable Angina.treatment: Antiplatelet + anticoagulation, anti-ischemic therapy, risk stratification (GRACE score); early invasive strategy (<24 h) for high risk, immediate (<2 h) for very high risk.
medications: Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC OD or Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD
NSTEMI / Unstable Angina.precautions: Dose-adjust enoxaparin in renal impairment. Dual antiplatelet therapy typically 12 months — balance bleeding risk; add PPI if GI risk.
emergency_flags: Hemodynamic instability with ischemic chest pain
High-risk GRACE score requiring immediate catheterization

Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Frac.name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)
Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Frac.symptoms: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion, orthopnea needing multiple pillows to sleep, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, bilateral pitting ankle edema, persistent dry or pink frothy cough, extreme fatigue, abdominal fullness
symptoms_list: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion
orthopnea needing multiple pillows to sleep
persistent dry or pink frothy cough
Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Frac.treatment: Four-pillar guideline-directed medical therapy, diuretics for congestion, device therapy (ICD/CRT) when EF ≤35% despite therapy, salt restriction, cardiac rehab.
medications: Bisoprolol 1.25–10 mg OD, Carvedilol 3.125–25 mg BD or Metoprolol succinate
Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD or Empagliflozin 10 mg OD
Ivabradine, hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in selected patients.
Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Frac.precautions: Monitor K⁺/creatinine. 36-hour washout between ACEi and sacubitril/valsartan (angioedema). Avoid NSAIDs, non-DHP CCBs, thiazolidinediones. Daily weights; IV iron if ferritin <100.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fr.name: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fr.symptoms: Exertional dyspnea, exercise intolerance, fatigue, bilateral lower leg swelling, rapid weight gain from fluid retention, elevated jugular venous pulsation in older hypertensive or diabetic patients
symptoms_list: rapid weight gain from fluid retention
elevated jugular venous pulsation in older hypertensive or diabetic patients
investigations: amyloid workup (technetium pyrophosphate scan, serum free light chains) where suspected.
Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fr.treatment: Diuretics for congestion, SGLT2 inhibitor, control BP, AF, obesity, diabetes; exercise training.
medications: Empagliflozin 10 mg OD or Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD
Finerenone (2024 FINEARTS-HF evidence) in selected patients
Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fr.precautions: Avoid over-diuresis (preload dependent). Check renal function and potassium with MRAs.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Decompensated Heart Failure / Acut.name: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure / Acute Pulmonary Edema
Acute Decompensated Heart Failure / Acut.symptoms: Acute severe respiratory distress, inability to lie flat, coughing copious pink frothy sputum, bilateral lung crackles, cold clammy extremities, cyanosis, severe agitation and air hunger
Acute Decompensated Heart Failure / Acut.treatment: Sit upright, oxygen/non-invasive ventilation (CPAP/BiPAP) if hypoxic, IV loop diuretics, vasodilators if BP adequate; inotropes if cardiogenic shock. Treat precipitant.
medications: Dobutamine 2–20 mcg/kg/min or Norepinephrine in shock
Acute Decompensated Heart Failure / Acut.precautions: Monitor urine output, electrolytes (hypokalemia), creatinine. Avoid nitrates in severe aortic stenosis/hypotension.
emergency_flags: Respiratory failure with pink frothy sputum

Atrial Fibrillation.name: Atrial Fibrillation
Atrial Fibrillation.symptoms: Irregularly irregular rapid heartbeat, fluttering palpitations in chest, sudden unexplained fatigue, dizziness, lightheadedness, exertional shortness of breath, mild chest tightness
investigations: TEE before cardioversion if AF >48 h without 3 weeks anticoagulation.
Atrial Fibrillation.treatment: Rate or rhythm control, stroke prevention by CHA₂DS₂-VA score, treat risk factors (alcohol, OSA, obesity, HTN). Urgent cardioversion if unstable; catheter ablation for symptomatic patients.
medications: Rate: Metoprolol 25–100 mg BD, Bisoprolol, Diltiazem 60–120 mg TDS

Digoxin 0.125–0.25 mg OD. Rhythm: Amiodarone, Flecainide (no structural disease), Dronedarone. Anticoagulation: Apixaban 5 mg BD (2.5 mg BD if 2 of: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, creatinine ≥1.5), Rivaroxaban 20 mg OD with food, Dabigatran 150 mg BD
Warfarin (INR 2–3) for mechanical valve/moderate–severe mitral stenosis.
Atrial Fibrillation.precautions: DOACs contraindicated with mechanical valves. Adjust for renal function. Avoid AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF (WPW). Amiodarone → thyroid, liver, lung, eye toxicity.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Atrial Fibrillation symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Atrial Flutter.name: Atrial Flutter
Atrial Flutter.symptoms: Regular rapid fluttering palpitations (heart rate around 150 bpm), fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, lightheadedness, mild chest discomfort
symptoms_list: Regular rapid fluttering palpitations (heart rate around 150 bpm)
investigations: ECG (sawtooth flutter waves, 2:1 block at ~150 bpm)
Atrial Flutter.treatment: Similar to AF: rate control, anticoagulation by stroke risk; cavotricuspid isthmus ablation is first-line definitive therapy (>90% success).
Atrial Flutter.precautions: Class IC drugs without AV-nodal blockers may cause 1:1 conduction. Anticoagulate before cardioversion as for AF.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Atrial Flutter symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia.name: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (AVNRT/AVRT)
Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia.symptoms: Sudden onset of rapid regular pounding palpitations (heart rate 160-220 bpm) starting and stopping abruptly, lightheadedness, neck fullness, anxiety, shortness of breath, polyuria after episode
symptoms_list: Sudden onset of rapid regular pounding palpitations (heart rate 160-220 bpm) starting and stopping abruptly
Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia.treatment: Vagal manoeuvres (modified Valsalva), then adenosine; synchronized cardioversion if unstable; catheter ablation for recurrent episodes.
medications: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push, then 12 mg (repeat 12 mg once)
Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia.precautions: Adenosine contraindicated in severe asthma; warn of transient chest discomfort. Avoid verapamil in broad-complex tachycardia or WPW with AF.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (AVNRT/AVRT) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Ventricular Tachycardia.name: Ventricular Tachycardia
Ventricular Tachycardia.symptoms: Sudden sustained racing heart, palpitations, lightheadedness, syncope or near-syncope, chest pain, shortness of breath, hemodynamic instability
Ventricular Tachycardia.treatment: Pulseless → ACLS defibrillation. Unstable with pulse → synchronized cardioversion. Stable → antiarrhythmic. ICD for secondary prevention; ablation for recurrent VT.
medications: Amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 min then 1 mg/min × 6 h, 0.5 mg/min × 18 h
Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV for torsades
Ventricular Tachycardia.precautions: Treat as VT if in doubt. Avoid QT-prolonging drugs. Correct K⁺ >4.0 and Mg²⁺ >2.0.

Ventricular Fibrillation / Cardiac Arres.name: Ventricular Fibrillation / Cardiac Arrest
Ventricular Fibrillation / Cardiac Arres.symptoms: Sudden collapse, unresponsiveness, absence of pulse and normal breathing, cardiac arrest, gasping agonal respirations
symptoms_list: absence of pulse and normal breathing
Ventricular Fibrillation / Cardiac Arres.treatment: High-quality CPR (100–120/min, 5–6 cm depth), early defibrillation, ACLS algorithm, airway, treat reversible causes (4 Hs & 4 Ts), post-arrest care with temperature control, coronary angiography.
medications: Amiodarone 300 mg IV after 3rd shock, then 150 mg
Ventricular Fibrillation / Cardiac Arres.precautions: Minimize interruptions in compressions (<10 s). Avoid hyperventilation and hyperoxia post-ROSC.
emergency_flags: Unresponsive patient with ventricular fibrillation or cardiac arrest
Immediate ACLS protocol and defibrillation required

Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome.name: Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome
Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome.symptoms: Persistent slow heart rate below 50 bpm, fatigue, chronic dizziness, near-syncope or blackout spells (Stokes-Adams attacks), exercise intolerance, confusion in elderly
symptoms_list: Persistent slow heart rate below 50 bpm
Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome.treatment: Asymptomatic → observe. Symptomatic → stop offending drugs, atropine, pacing; permanent pacemaker for symptomatic sinus node dysfunction.
medications: Atropine 1 mg IV q3–5 min (max 3 mg)
Dopamine 5–20 mcg/kg/min or Epinephrine 2–10 mcg/min infusion
Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome.precautions: Atropine ineffective in heart transplant and infranodal blocks. Review all rate-slowing drugs.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Complete (Third-degree) Heart Block.name: Complete (Third-degree) Heart Block
Complete (Third-degree) Heart Block.symptoms: Profound bradycardia (heart rate 30-40 bpm), recurrent fainting spells (syncope), severe lightheadedness, marked fatigue, dyspnea on minimal exertion, cannon A waves in neck
Complete (Third-degree) Heart Block.treatment: Temporary transcutaneous/transvenous pacing if unstable, then permanent dual-chamber pacemaker. Treat reversible causes (inferior MI, Lyme, drugs, hyperkalemia).
medications: Atropine 1 mg IV (often ineffective), Isoprenaline infusion, Dopamine or Epinephrine as bridge.
Complete (Third-degree) Heart Block.precautions: Avoid AV-nodal blocking agents. Monitor for asystole; keep pacing pads on.
emergency_flags: Severe symptomatic bradycardia with syncope or hemodynamic instability

Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome.name: Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome
Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome.symptoms: Episodic rapid regular palpitations, sudden tachycardia, dizziness, syncope in young patients, ECG showing short PR interval and delta wave
symptoms_list: ECG showing short PR interval and delta wave
Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome.treatment: Catheter ablation of accessory pathway is curative. Acute orthodromic AVRT: vagal manoeuvres/adenosine. Pre-excited AF: procainamide or cardioversion.
medications: Flecainide/Propafenone long-term if ablation not possible.
Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome.precautions: Never give adenosine, digoxin, verapamil, diltiazem or beta-blockers in pre-excited AF (risk of VF).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Long QT Syndrome.name: Long QT Syndrome
Long QT Syndrome.symptoms: Recurrent unexplained fainting (syncope) triggered by emotional stress, sudden loud noise, or swimming; palpitations, family history of sudden cardiac arrest
symptoms_list: Recurrent unexplained fainting (syncope) triggered by emotional stress
family history of sudden cardiac arrest
Long QT Syndrome.treatment: Beta-blockade, avoid QT-prolonging drugs, correct electrolytes; ICD for cardiac arrest survivors/high risk; left cardiac sympathetic denervation.
medications: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV for torsades
Long QT Syndrome.precautions: Check crediblemeds.org list before prescribing (macrolides, fluoroquinolones, antipsychotics, ondansetron). Avoid sudden loud noises/swimming per genotype.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Long QT Syndrome symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.name: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.symptoms: Dyspnea on exertion, atypical chest pain, exertional dizziness or syncope, palpitations, systolic ejection murmur that increases with Valsalva maneuver
symptoms_list: systolic ejection murmur that increases with Valsalva maneuver
Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.treatment: Beta-blocker/non-DHP CCB for symptoms; cardiac myosin inhibitor for obstructive HCM; septal myectomy/alcohol septal ablation for refractory obstruction; ICD for high SCD risk.
Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.precautions: Avoid dehydration, vasodilators, nitrates and high-dose diuretics in obstruction. Avoid competitive strenuous sport until assessed. Mavacamten: REMS-type EF monitoring, CYP interactions.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Dilated Cardiomyopathy.name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
Dilated Cardiomyopathy.symptoms: Progressive exercise intolerance, fatigue, shortness of breath, orthopnea, bilateral lower limb edema, abdominal distension, history of viral illness or heavy alcohol use
symptoms_list: history of viral illness or heavy alcohol use
Dilated Cardiomyopathy.treatment: As HFrEF GDMT; treat cause (alcohol, viral, peripartum, tachycardia-induced); ICD/CRT; heart transplant/LVAD for end stage.
medications: anticoagulation if AF or LV thrombus.
Dilated Cardiomyopathy.precautions: Strict alcohol abstinence; avoid cardiotoxic drugs (anthracyclines, trastuzumab without monitoring).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Dilated Cardiomyopathy symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Pericarditis.name: Acute Pericarditis
Acute Pericarditis.symptoms: Sharp pleuritic retrosternal chest pain aggravated by deep inspiration and coughing, pain relieved by sitting up and leaning forward, low-grade fever, pericardial friction rub
symptoms_list: Sharp pleuritic retrosternal chest pain aggravated by deep inspiration and coughing
pain relieved by sitting up and leaning forward
Acute Pericarditis.treatment: NSAID + colchicine, rest from strenuous activity until resolution; treat cause.
medications: Ibuprofen 600–800 mg TDS or Aspirin 750–1000 mg TDS for 1–2 weeks then taper
Colchicine 0.5 mg BD (0.5 mg OD if <70 kg) for 3 months
Prednisone low dose only if NSAID contraindicated.
Acute Pericarditis.precautions: Avoid steroids as first line (increase recurrence). Avoid NSAIDs post-MI (use aspirin). Restrict sport 3 months in myopericarditis.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Acute Pericarditis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Pericardial Effusion / Cardiac Tamponade.name: Pericardial Effusion / Cardiac Tamponade
Pericardial Effusion / Cardiac Tamponade.symptoms: Severe dyspnea, orthopnea, distant or muffled heart sounds, elevated jugular venous pressure, systemic hypotension (Beck triad), pulsus paradoxus, cold clammy skin
investigations: pericardial fluid analysis (cell count, ADA, cytology, culture).
Pericardial Effusion / Cardiac Tamponade.treatment: Tamponade → urgent echo-guided pericardiocentesis; IV fluids temporarily. Treat underlying cause. Pericardial window for recurrent effusions.
medications: cause-specific (NSAID/colchicine, antitubercular therapy, chemotherapy for malignant effusion).
Pericardial Effusion / Cardiac Tamponade.precautions: Avoid diuretics, vasodilators and positive-pressure ventilation in tamponade.
emergency_flags: Cardiac tamponade with Beck triad (hypotension, muffled heart sounds, elevated JVP)

Constrictive Pericarditis.name: Constrictive Pericarditis
Constrictive Pericarditis.symptoms: Chronic fatigue, exertional dyspnea, marked ascites out of proportion to peripheral edema, hepatic enlargement, elevated JVP with prominent Y descent (Kussmaul sign)
symptoms_list: marked ascites out of proportion to peripheral edema
elevated JVP with prominent Y descent (Kussmaul sign)
Constrictive Pericarditis.treatment: Diuretics for congestion; anti-inflammatory therapy for transient constriction; pericardiectomy for chronic constriction; antitubercular therapy if TB.
Constrictive Pericarditis.precautions: Over-diuresis worsens output. TB is a leading cause in India/Africa — screen.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Constrictive Pericarditis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Myocarditis.name: Acute Myocarditis
Acute Myocarditis.symptoms: Recent flu-like illness followed by sudden chest pain mimicking infarction, breathlessness, fatigue, palpitations, acute heart failure symptoms in young adults
symptoms_list: Recent flu-like illness followed by sudden chest pain mimicking infarction
acute heart failure symptoms in young adults
Acute Myocarditis.treatment: Supportive care, heart failure therapy, arrhythmia management; mechanical support in fulminant cases; immunosuppression for giant-cell/eosinophilic/sarcoid myocarditis.
medications: Corticosteroids ± other immunosuppressants for specific histology.
Acute Myocarditis.precautions: Avoid NSAIDs in myocarditis (unlike pericarditis). Avoid competitive sport for 3–6 months.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Acute Myocarditis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Infective Endocarditis.name: Infective Endocarditis
Infective Endocarditis.symptoms: Prolonged remittent fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, new or changing heart murmur, petechiae, splinter hemorrhages under nails, Osler nodes, Janeway lesions
investigations: ≥3 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics
Infective Endocarditis.treatment: Prolonged IV bactericidal antibiotics (4–6 weeks), surgery for heart failure, uncontrolled infection, large vegetations with emboli.
medications: Empirical (native valve): Ampicillin + (Flucloxacillin or Cefazolin) + Gentamicin, or Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h + Gentamicin if MRSA risk. Strep viridans: Penicillin G 12–18 MU/day or Ceftriaxone 2 g OD × 4 weeks. MSSA: Flucloxacillin 2 g q4h or Cefazolin. Enterococcus: Ampicillin + Ceftriaxone.
Infective Endocarditis.precautions: Monitor vancomycin/gentamicin levels and renal function, audiometry. Dental hygiene; prophylaxis before dental procedures for prosthetic valves/prior IE.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Infective Endocarditis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Rheumatic Fever.name: Acute Rheumatic Fever
Acute Rheumatic Fever.symptoms: Migratory polyarthritis affecting large joints, high fever, subcutaneous nodules, erythema marginatum rash, Sydenham chorea, history of untreated sore throat 2-3 weeks prior
symptoms_list: history of untreated sore throat 2-3 weeks prior
Acute Rheumatic Fever.treatment: Eradicate streptococci, anti-inflammatory therapy, bed rest in carditis, secondary prophylaxis.
medications: Benzathine penicillin G 1.2 MU IM single dose (or Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg OD × 10 days)
Haloperidol/Valproate for chorea. Prophylaxis: Benzathine penicillin every 3–4 weeks (5–10 years or to age 40 with RHD).
Acute Rheumatic Fever.precautions: Avoid aspirin in viral illness in children (Reye syndrome) — monitor. Penicillin allergy → erythromycin/azithromycin.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Acute Rheumatic Fever symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis.name: Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis.symptoms: Exertional dyspnea, fatigue, orthopnea, hemoptysis (pulmonary apoplexy), palpitations due to atrial fibrillation, malar flush (mitral facies), low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur
Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis.treatment: Rate control, anticoagulation if AF, diuretics; percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy for favourable anatomy; surgical repair/replacement otherwise. Secondary penicillin prophylaxis.
medications: Beta-blockers or Ivabradine (slows HR, prolongs diastole)
Warfarin INR 2–3 if AF/thrombus (DOACs not recommended in moderate-severe MS)
Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis.precautions: Pregnancy is high risk — counsel. Avoid tachycardia.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Aortic Stenosis.name: Aortic Stenosis
Aortic Stenosis.symptoms: Classic triad of exertional dyspnea, angina pectoris, and syncope upon physical exertion; harsh systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur radiating to carotids
symptoms_list: harsh systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur radiating to carotids
investigations: Echo (AVA <1.0 cm², mean gradient >40 mmHg, Vmax >4 m/s)
Aortic Stenosis.treatment: Watchful waiting if asymptomatic; aortic valve replacement (TAVI or SAVR) when severe and symptomatic or EF <50%.
medications: No drug alters progression. Cautious diuretics
Aortic Stenosis.precautions: Avoid vasodilators/nitrates and dehydration in severe AS. Syncope/angina/dyspnea → urgent referral.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Aortic Stenosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Aortic Regurgitation.name: Aortic Regurgitation
Aortic Regurgitation.symptoms: Exertional dyspnea, awareness of pounding heartbeat in chest and neck, wide pulse pressure (water-hammer pulse), head nodding with heartbeats, early diastolic decrescendo murmur
symptoms_list: awareness of pounding heartbeat in chest and neck
Aortic Regurgitation.treatment: Treat cause; vasodilators for hypertension; surgery if symptomatic, LVEF ≤55% or LV end-systolic dimension >50 mm.
medications: ACEi/ARB or Dihydropyridine CCB (Nifedipine) for BP
Aortic Regurgitation.precautions: Acute severe AR (dissection/endocarditis) is a surgical emergency. Avoid bradycardia-inducing drugs in chronic AR.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Aortic Regurgitation symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Mitral Regurgitation.name: Mitral Regurgitation
Mitral Regurgitation.symptoms: Fatigue, exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations from atrial fibrillation, holosystolic murmur at cardiac apex radiating to the left axilla
symptoms_list: holosystolic murmur at cardiac apex radiating to the left axilla
Mitral Regurgitation.treatment: Primary MR: surgical repair if symptomatic or LV dysfunction. Secondary MR: optimize HF therapy, CRT, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
Mitral Regurgitation.precautions: Acute MR after MI (papillary muscle rupture) → emergency surgery.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Mitral Regurgitation symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Mitral Valve Prolapse.name: Mitral Valve Prolapse
Mitral Valve Prolapse.hindi_names: Heart ka valve dheela hona; MVP
Mitral Valve Prolapse.symptoms: Systolic click and late systolic murmur on auscultation; Often asymptomatic; Mid-chest atypical pain; Palpitations; Lightheadedness; Anxiety; Fatigue; Dyspnea; Panic attacks
symptoms_list: Systolic click and late systolic murmur on auscultation
clarifying_questions: 1. Echo test me Mitral Valve Prolapse (MVP) aaya hai?
2. Chhati me dhak-dhak ya halka dard hota hai?
3. Ghabraahat hoti hai?
investigations: Echocardiography with Doppler (assess degree of mitral regurgitation and leaflet displacement)
Mitral Valve Prolapse.treatment: Avoid excess caffeine, alcohol, and dehydration; Regular low-impact aerobic exercise; Reassurance regarding benign nature
medications: Reassurance + Metoprolol OR Propranolol (if symptomatic palpitations)
Antibiotic prophylaxis NO LONGER routinely required for dental work
Mitral Valve Prolapse.generic_drug: Reassurance + Metoprolol OR Propranolol (if symptomatic palpitations)
Mitral Valve Prolapse.supportive_medicines: Anxiolytics short-term; Hydration; Antibiotic prophylaxis NO LONGER routinely required for dental work

Aortic Dissection.name: Aortic Dissection
Aortic Dissection.symptoms: Sudden onset of excruciating tearing or ripping chest pain radiating through to the upper back and interscapular region, pulse asymmetry between arms, neurological deficits, severe hypertension or shock
symptoms_list: Sudden onset of excruciating tearing or ripping chest pain radiating through to the upper back and interscapular region
Aortic Dissection.treatment: Type A → emergency surgery. Type B uncomplicated → medical (anti-impulse) therapy; complicated → TEVAR.
medications: IV Esmolol (500 mcg/kg bolus then 50–300 mcg/kg/min) or Labetalol to HR <60 and SBP 100–120 mmHg within 20 min
Aortic Dissection.precautions: Never thrombolyse. Beta-block before vasodilator (avoid reflex tachycardia).
emergency_flags: Tearing chest pain radiating to back
Pulse or blood pressure asymmetry between limbs

Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.symptoms: Often asymptomatic pulsatile abdominal mass near umbilicus; or sudden severe constant abdominal and back pain with hypotension indicating rupture
symptoms_list: Often asymptomatic pulsatile abdominal mass near umbilicus
or sudden severe constant abdominal and back pain with hypotension indicating rupture
investigations: Abdominal USG (screening men 65–75 who ever smoked)
Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.treatment: Surveillance for small AAA; elective repair (open or EVAR) at ≥5.5 cm men/≥5.0 cm women or growth >1 cm/year; emergency repair if rupture.
medications: smoking cessation (no drug slows growth reliably).
Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.precautions: Ruptured AAA — permissive hypotension (SBP 70–90) before repair. Avoid fluoroquinolones (possible aneurysm risk).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Peripheral Arterial Disease.name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
Peripheral Arterial Disease.symptoms: Intermittent claudication (cramping pain in calf, thigh, or buttock induced by walking and relieved within minutes by rest), cold pale feet, diminished peripheral pulses, slow wound healing
symptoms_list: or buttock induced by walking and relieved within minutes by rest)
Peripheral Arterial Disease.treatment: Smoking cessation, supervised exercise, risk-factor control, revascularization for critical limb ischemia or lifestyle-limiting claudication.
medications: Aspirin 75–100 mg or Clopidogrel 75 mg OD
Rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD + aspirin (COMPASS) in selected
Peripheral Arterial Disease.precautions: Cilostazol contraindicated in heart failure. Foot care; avoid tight footwear.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Peripheral Arterial Disease symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Limb Ischemia.name: Acute Limb Ischemia
Acute Limb Ischemia.symptoms: Acute onset of severe extremity pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesias, poikilothermia (cold limb), and paralysis (the 6 Ps of acute limb ischemia)
symptoms_list: Acute onset of severe extremity pain
and paralysis (the 6 Ps of acute limb ischemia)
Acute Limb Ischemia.treatment: Immediate heparin, urgent vascular surgery (embolectomy, catheter-directed thrombolysis, bypass); fasciotomy for compartment syndrome; amputation if non-viable.
medications: Unfractionated heparin 80 U/kg bolus then 18 U/kg/h
Acute Limb Ischemia.precautions: "6 Ps": treat within 6 h. Watch reperfusion hyperkalemia and myoglobinuria.
emergency_flags: Acute limb ischemia (6 Ps: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesias, Poikilothermia, Paralysis)

Deep Vein Thrombosis.name: Deep Vein Thrombosis
Deep Vein Thrombosis.symptoms: Unilateral calf or thigh swelling, localized calf warmth, erythema, tenderness along deep veins, pain aggravated by dorsiflexion of foot (Homan sign)
symptoms_list: pain aggravated by dorsiflexion of foot (Homan sign)
Deep Vein Thrombosis.treatment: Anticoagulation ≥3 months (provoked) or extended (unprovoked/cancer); compression for symptoms; catheter thrombolysis for limb-threatening DVT.
medications: Apixaban 10 mg BD × 7 days then 5 mg BD
Rivaroxaban 15 mg BD × 21 days then 20 mg OD
Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD (bridge to warfarin INR 2–3 or dabigatran)
Deep Vein Thrombosis.precautions: Avoid DOACs in antiphospholipid syndrome (triple positive), pregnancy, severe renal impairment. Watch bleeding.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Deep Vein Thrombosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Pulmonary Embolism.name: Pulmonary Embolism
Pulmonary Embolism.symptoms: Sudden acute pleuritic chest pain, unexplained shortness of breath, tachypnea, tachycardia, hemoptysis, lightheadedness, syncope in patients with risk factors like immobility or surgery
symptoms_list: syncope in patients with risk factors like immobility or surgery
Pulmonary Embolism.treatment: Anticoagulation; systemic thrombolysis for high-risk (shock); catheter-directed therapy for intermediate-high risk deteriorating; IVC filter if anticoagulation contraindicated.
medications: LMWH or UFH (UFH if thrombolysis likely)
Alteplase 100 mg IV over 2 h for massive PE.
Pulmonary Embolism.precautions: Do not delay anticoagulation if high suspicion. Thrombolysis contraindications: recent surgery, stroke, bleeding.
emergency_flags: Massive pulmonary embolism with shock or severe hypotension

Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insuffic.name: Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insufficiency
Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insuffic.symptoms: Aching leg heaviness, lower leg swelling worsened by prolonged standing, visibly dilated tortuous veins, stasis dermatitis, skin hyperpigmentation, medial malleolus venous ulcers
symptoms_list: lower leg swelling worsened by prolonged standing
Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insuffic.treatment: Compression stockings, leg elevation, exercise, weight loss; endovenous laser/radiofrequency ablation, sclerotherapy, surgery.
medications: Micronized purified flavonoid fraction (Diosmin-hesperidin) 1000 mg/day for symptoms
Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insuffic.precautions: Do not apply compression if ABI <0.8 (arterial disease). Skin care to prevent ulcers.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insufficiency symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Superficial Thrombophlebitis.name: Superficial Thrombophlebitis
Superficial Thrombophlebitis.symptoms: Painful, tender, erythematous cord-like induration along a superficial vein of the lower or upper limb, localized warmth and swelling without deep calf edema
symptoms_list: erythematous cord-like induration along a superficial vein of the lower or upper limb
localized warmth and swelling without deep calf edema
Superficial Thrombophlebitis.treatment: Warm compress, compression, NSAIDs; anticoagulation if ≥5 cm length or near saphenofemoral junction.
medications: Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC OD × 45 days for extensive thrombosis.
Superficial Thrombophlebitis.precautions: Within 3 cm of SFJ → treat as DVT.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Superficial Thrombophlebitis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.

Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia).name: Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia)
Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia).symptoms: Usually asymptomatic silent lipid elevation; in severe familial cases tendon xanthomas on Achilles tendon, xanthelasma around eyelids, corneal arcus before age 50
symptoms_list: in severe familial cases tendon xanthomas on Achilles tendon
Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia).treatment: Diet (reduce saturated/trans fat), exercise, weight loss; statin intensity according to ASCVD risk; LDL targets <55 mg/dL very high risk, <70 high risk, <100 moderate.
medications: Atorvastatin 10–80 mg OD, Rosuvastatin 5–40 mg OD
PCSK9 inhibitors (Evolocumab 140 mg SC q2w, Alirocumab), Inclisiran 284 mg SC at 0, 3 months then 6-monthly
Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia).precautions: Statins contraindicated in pregnancy. Check for myopathy; avoid simvastatin with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Check LFT at baseline.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypertriglyceridemia.name: Hypertriglyceridemia
Hypertriglyceridemia.hindi_names: High Triglycerides; High Fat in Blood
Hypertriglyceridemia.symptoms: Elevated Serum Triglycerides (>150-200 mg/dL; Severe >500 mg/dL); Asymptomatic; Eruptive xanthomas (if >1000 mg/dL); Lipemia retinalis; Hepatosplenomegaly; Acute Pancreatitis risk (when TG >500-1000 mg/dL)
clarifying_questions: 1. Fasting lipid report me Triglycerides kitne hain (>200 ya >500)?
2. Alcohol, sweets, ya oily food zyada khate hain?

Hypertriglyceridemia.treatment: STRICT ZERO ALCOHOL; Eliminate refined sugars, sweets, fruit juices, and refined carbs; Low-fat diet; Weight loss; Exercise daily

Bronchial Asthma.name: Bronchial Asthma
Bronchial Asthma.symptoms: Recurrent episodes of expiratory wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, chronic dry cough especially at night or early morning, triggered by cold air, exercise, or dust
symptoms_list: chronic dry cough especially at night or early morning
investigations: Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility (≥12% and 200 mL FEV₁)
Bronchial Asthma.treatment: Stepwise GINA approach. Preferred track: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (Steps 1–2), maintenance and reliever therapy (MART) at Steps 3–4, add-on LAMA/biologics at Step 5. Avoid SABA-only therapy. Inhaler technique, trigger avoidance, action plan.
medications: Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg 1 puff PRN (max 12/day) or 1–2 puffs BD as MART
Biologics (Omalizumab, Mepolizumab, Benralizumab, Dupilumab, Tezepelumab) for severe asthma.
Bronchial Asthma.precautions: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers and aspirin/NSAIDs in aspirin-exacerbated disease. Rinse mouth after ICS (thrush). Montelukast → neuropsychiatric warning.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Bronchial Asthma symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Severe Asthma (Status Asthmaticus).name: Acute Severe Asthma (Status Asthmaticus)
Acute Severe Asthma (Status Asthmaticus).symptoms: Severe unrelenting respiratory distress, inability to complete full sentences in one breath, tachypnea > 30 breaths/min, intercostal retractions, silent chest on auscultation, cyanosis, exhaustion
symptoms_list: inability to complete full sentences in one breath
Acute Severe Asthma (Status Asthmaticus).treatment: Oxygen to SpO₂ 93–95%, repeated bronchodilators, systemic steroids, IV magnesium; ICU/intubation if exhaustion, silent chest, rising CO₂.
medications: Salbutamol 2.5–5 mg nebulized every 20 min × 3 (or continuous)
Prednisolone 40–50 mg PO or Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV q6h × 5–7 days
Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 20 min
Acute Severe Asthma (Status Asthmaticus).precautions: Sedatives contraindicated outside ICU. Monitor potassium. Normal PaCO₂ in a breathless asthmatic = impending failure.
emergency_flags: PaCO2 normal or rising in breathless patient indicates impending failure

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.symptoms: Progressive exertional breathlessness, chronic productive cough with morning sputum, audible wheezing, frequent chest infections, barrel chest, prolonged expiratory phase, history of smoking
symptoms_list: chronic productive cough with morning sputum
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.treatment: Smoking cessation, vaccination (influenza, pneumococcal, RSV, Tdap), pulmonary rehabilitation, bronchodilators per GOLD group, long-term oxygen if PaO₂ ≤55 mmHg, NIV for chronic hypercapnia.
medications: add ICS (triple therapy) if eosinophils ≥300 or frequent exacerbations
Azithromycin 250 mg OD/500 mg 3×/week for exacerbators
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (C.precautions: Oxygen target 88–92% (risk of CO₂ retention). ICS increases pneumonia risk. Azithromycin → QT prolongation, hearing loss.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Exacerbation of COPD.name: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
Acute Exacerbation of COPD.symptoms: Acute worsening of baseline dyspnea, increased volume and purulence (yellow/green) of sputum, increased coughing, fever, wheezing in a known COPD patient
symptoms_list: increased volume and purulence (yellow/green) of sputum
wheezing in a known COPD patient
Acute Exacerbation of COPD.treatment: Controlled oxygen, short-acting bronchodilators, systemic steroids, antibiotics if increased sputum purulence; NIV for acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis (pH <7.35).
medications: Antibiotics 5 days: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 625 mg TDS, Doxycycline 100 mg BD or Azithromycin
Acute Exacerbation of COPD.precautions: Target SpO₂ 88–92%; monitor glucose on steroids.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Acute Exacerbation of COPD symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Community-Acquired Pneumonia.name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
Community-Acquired Pneumonia.symptoms: High fever with shaking chills (rigors), productive cough with purulent or rust-colored sputum, localized pleuritic chest pain worsened by deep breathing, tachypnea, crackles on auscultation
clarifying_questions: 1. Khansi me hara ya lal balgam aata hai?
2. Saans lene me chhati me dard hota hai?

Community-Acquired Pneumonia.treatment: Strict bed rest; High calorie high protein diet; Hydration; Deep breathing exercises
Community-Acquired Pneumonia.supportive_medicines: Paracetamol 650 mg SOS; Expectorant syrup; Oxygen therapy if hypoxemic

medication_card.generic_drug: Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid
medication_card.precautions: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Penicillin allergy; Severe renal failure (adjust dose); Caution in elderly

High calorie high protein diet

Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associate.name: Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associate.symptoms: New fever, purulent endotracheal secretions or sputum, worsening hypoxemia, new pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray appearing 48 hours or more after hospital admission
symptoms_list: new pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray appearing 48 hours or more after hospital admission
Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associate.treatment: Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics based on local antibiogram and MDR risk; de-escalate with cultures; 7 days usually.
medications: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h, Cefepime 2 g q8h or Meropenem 1 g q8h
add Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h or Linezolid 600 mg BD for MRSA
second anti-pseudomonal agent (Amikacin) if high risk
Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associate.precautions: Head-of-bed elevation 30–45°, daily sedation holds, oral care. Monitor renal function with vancomycin/aminoglycosides/colistin.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia symptoms.

Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess.name: Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess
Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess.symptoms: Fever, night sweats, weight loss, cough productive of foul-smelling putrid sputum, history of impaired consciousness, alcohol intoxication, or swallowing difficulty
symptoms_list: cough productive of foul-smelling putrid sputum
Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess.treatment: Antibiotics, postural drainage, treat dysphagia/dental disease; percutaneous drainage/surgery for non-resolving abscess.
medications: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1.2 g IV TDS or Ampicillin-sulbactam
Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess.precautions: Aspiration pneumonitis (chemical) often needs no antibiotics initially. Nil by mouth until swallow evaluated.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.

Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible.name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible)
Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible.symptoms: Chronic productive cough lasting over 3 weeks, hemoptysis (blood in sputum), low-grade evening fever, drenching night sweats, unexplained weight loss, anorexia, fatigue
symptoms_list: Chronic productive cough lasting over 3 weeks
investigations: CBNAAT/Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (also detects rifampicin resistance)
Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible.treatment: Directly observed/supported therapy under national programme (NTEP in India). Standard 6-month regimen 2HRZE/4HR; 4-month HPZM regimen (isoniazid, rifapentine, pyrazinamide, moxifloxacin) for ≥12 years per 2025 ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA and WHO; 4-month 2HRZ(E)/2HR for children with non-severe TB.
medications: Weight-band fixed-dose combinations: Isoniazid 5 mg/kg, Rifampicin 10 mg/kg, Pyrazinamide 25 mg/kg, Ethambutol 15 mg/kg daily
Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible.precautions: Hepatotoxicity (H, R, Z) — monitor LFT; stop if ALT >3× with symptoms or >5×. Rifampicin reduces OCP, warfarin, ART efficacy; turns urine orange. Ethambutol → optic neuritis. Notify cases.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB).name: Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB)
Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB).symptoms: Persistent chronic cough, hemoptysis, non-responsive to first-line anti-TB medications, progressive weight loss, continuous night sweats, severe lung damage
Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB).treatment: Specialist centre; 6-month all-oral BPaLM (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) for ≥14 years with fluoroquinolone-susceptible RR-TB; BPaL if fluoroquinolone-resistant; WHO 2025 alternatives include BDLLfxC; longer individualized regimens otherwise.
medications: Bedaquiline 400 mg OD × 2 weeks then 200 mg 3×/week
Moxifloxacin 400 mg OD — all for 26 weeks.
Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB).precautions: QT prolongation (bedaquiline + moxifloxacin), linezolid → anemia, thrombocytopenia, peripheral/optic neuropathy, lactic acidosis. Contact tracing.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) symptoms.

Latent Tuberculosis Infection.name: Latent Tuberculosis Infection
Latent Tuberculosis Infection.symptoms: Asymptomatic latent infection with positive tuberculin skin test (Mantoux) or IGRA, normal chest radiography, no cough, no night sweats, no weight loss
symptoms_list: Asymptomatic latent infection with positive tuberculin skin test (Mantoux) or IGRA
investigations: CXR and symptom screen to exclude active TB

medications: 3HP: Isoniazid 900 mg + Rifapentine 900 mg weekly × 12 weeks
Latent Tuberculosis Infection.precautions: Rule out active disease first (avoid monotherapy resistance). Rifamycin drug interactions.

Cystic Fibrosis.name: Cystic Fibrosis
Cystic Fibrosis.symptoms: Recurrent severe chest infections with Pseudomonas, chronic sinusitis, nasal polyps, malabsorption, greasy bulky foul-smelling stools, failure to thrive in childhood, salty-tasting skin
symptoms_list: Recurrent severe chest infections with Pseudomonas
Cystic Fibrosis.treatment: Multidisciplinary: airway clearance, CFTR modulators, nutrition, pancreatic enzyme replacement, infection control, transplant for end stage.

Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.symptoms: Insidious progressive exertional breathlessness, persistent dry hacking cough, bilateral dry inspiratory 'velcro' crackles at lung bases, digital clubbing in older adults
symptoms_list: bilateral dry inspiratory 'velcro' crackles at lung bases
investigations: autoimmune serology (ANA, RF, anti-CCP, myositis panel)
Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.treatment: Antifibrotics, pulmonary rehab, oxygen, vaccinations, treat GERD; lung transplant referral; palliative care.
medications: Nintedanib 150 mg BD or Pirfenidone 801 mg TDS (titrated)
Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.precautions: Nintedanib → diarrhea, LFT rise, bleeding risk. Pirfenidone → photosensitivity, take with food. Monitor LFTs monthly initially.

Sarcoidosis.name: Sarcoidosis
Sarcoidosis.symptoms: Persistent dry cough, exertional shortness of breath, fatigue, erythema nodosum (tender red shins), bilateral ankle swelling, anterior uveitis, blurred vision, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
Sarcoidosis.treatment: Observation for asymptomatic stage I/II; treat if organ-threatening (cardiac, neuro, ocular, renal, hypercalcemia) or symptomatic pulmonary disease.
medications: Prednisolone 20–40 mg OD tapered over 6–12 months
Sarcoidosis.precautions: Exclude TB before steroids in endemic regions. Bone protection on steroids.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Sarcoidosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.name: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis
Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.symptoms: Acute dyspnea, dry cough, fever, chills, malaise 4-8 hours after exposure to bird droppings or mold; or insidious breathlessness and weight loss in chronic exposure
symptoms_list: malaise 4-8 hours after exposure to bird droppings or mold
or insidious breathlessness and weight loss in chronic exposure
Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.treatment: Antigen identification and avoidance (birds, molds, humidifiers); corticosteroids for symptomatic or fibrotic disease; antifibrotics for progressive fibrosis.
medications: Mycophenolate mofetil or Azathioprine as steroid-sparing
Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.precautions: Complete antigen avoidance is essential; steroids alone do not halt disease if exposure continues.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Pneumothorax.name: Pneumothorax
Pneumothorax.symptoms: Sudden onset of sharp unilateral pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness; in tension pneumothorax severe cyanosis, hypotension, tracheal deviation away from affected side
symptoms_list: Sudden onset of sharp unilateral pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness
tracheal deviation away from affected side
Pneumothorax.treatment: Small primary, minimal symptoms → observation/outpatient; large or symptomatic → needle aspiration or small-bore chest drain; tension → immediate needle decompression (2nd ICS MCL or 4th/5th ICS AAL) then drain; recurrent → pleurodesis/VATS.
Pneumothorax.precautions: No air travel until resolved (1–2 weeks after resolution); no scuba diving lifelong unless definitive surgery. Smoking cessation.
emergency_flags: Tension pneumothorax with tracheal deviation and hypotension

Pleural Effusion.name: Pleural Effusion
Pleural Effusion.symptoms: Progressive exertional dyspnea, dullness to percussion, decreased breath sounds and vocal resonance at lung base, pleuritic chest pain in inflammatory effusions
symptoms_list: decreased breath sounds and vocal resonance at lung base
pleuritic chest pain in inflammatory effusions
Pleural Effusion.treatment: Treat cause; therapeutic thoracentesis if symptomatic; chest drain for empyema/complicated parapneumonic effusion; indwelling pleural catheter or pleurodesis for malignant effusion.
medications: Cause-specific: diuretics for heart failure, antibiotics for parapneumonic, ATT for tuberculous, intrapleural tPA + DNase for loculated empyema.
Pleural Effusion.precautions: Remove ≤1.5 L at a time (re-expansion pulmonary edema). USG guidance reduces pneumothorax risk.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Pleural Effusion symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Empyema.name: Empyema
Empyema.symptoms: High swinging fever, rigors, pleural chest pain, persistent cough, malaise, failure of pneumonia to resolve, thick purulent pleural fluid
Empyema.treatment: Chest tube drainage + prolonged antibiotics (3–6 weeks); intrapleural fibrinolytics; VATS decortication if fails.
medications: intrapleural Alteplase 10 mg + Dornase 5 mg BD × 3 days (MIST-2).
Empyema.precautions: Do not delay drainage; aminoglycosides penetrate pleura poorly.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Empyema symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARD.name: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARD.symptoms: Rapidly worsening severe shortness of breath, profound hypoxemia refractory to oxygen, tachypnea, diffuse bilateral crackles, confusion following sepsis, trauma, or severe pneumonia
symptoms_list: Rapidly worsening severe shortness of breath
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARD.treatment: Treat cause; lung-protective ventilation (tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight, plateau <30 cmH₂O), higher PEEP, prone positioning ≥16 h/day if P/F <150, conservative fluids; ECMO in refractory.
medications: Neuromuscular blockade (Cisatracurium) early in severe ARDS selectively
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARD.precautions: Avoid fluid overload; monitor for barotrauma; VAP prevention bundle.
emergency_flags: Severe refractory hypoxemia requiring lung-protective mechanical ventilation

Obstructive Sleep Apnea.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Obstructive Sleep Apnea.symptoms: Loud habitual snoring; Observed nocturnal apnea/gasping; Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS); Morning headache; Unrefreshing sleep; Impaired concentration; Nocturia; Irritability
clarifying_questions: 1. Raat ko kharraate aate hain aur saans achanak rukti hai?
2. Din me baith-baith kar neend aati hai?
3. Subah uthte hi sirdard rehta hai?
Obstructive Sleep Apnea.treatment: Weight reduction; Side-sleeping position (positional therapy); Avoid alcohol and sedatives before bedtime; CPAP compliance
medications: CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure) therapy - No primary drug
Modafinil 100 mg OD (only for residual daytime sleepiness under specialist guidance)
Obstructive Sleep Apnea.generic_drug: CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure) therapy - No primary drug
Obstructive Sleep Apnea.supportive_medicines: Modafinil 100 mg OD (only for residual daytime sleepiness under specialist guidance); Weight loss therapy

supportive_medicines: Modafinil 100 mg OD (only for residual daytime sleepiness under specialist guidance)

CPAP compliance

Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.name: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.symptoms: Progressive breathlessness on exertion, fatigue, lightheadedness, exertional syncope, peripheral edema, loud P2 heart sound, tricuspid regurgitation murmur
differential_diagnoses: PH due to left heart disease
investigations: right heart catheterization (mPAP >20 mmHg, PVR >2 WU, PAWP ≤15)
Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.treatment: Specialist centre; risk stratification; initial dual oral therapy for most; add parenteral prostacyclin for high risk; oxygen, diuretics, anticoagulation selected, transplant.
medications: Ambrisentan 5–10 mg OD or Macitentan 10 mg OD (ERA) + Tadalafil 40 mg OD or Sildenafil 20 mg TDS (PDE5i)
high-dose CCB only in vasoreactive patients.
Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.precautions: ERAs teratogenic — contraception and pregnancy tests. No nitrates with PDE5i. Pregnancy contraindicated.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell).name: Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell)
Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell).symptoms: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, unresolving pneumonia, localized chest pain, hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, unexplained weight loss, finger clubbing in smokers
symptoms_list: hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy
investigations: molecular testing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK, HER2)
Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell).treatment: Staging-dependent: surgery (lobectomy) for early stage ± adjuvant/perioperative chemo-immunotherapy or Osimertinib (EGFR); chemoradiation + Durvalumab for stage III; targeted therapy or immunotherapy ± chemotherapy for stage IV based on biomarkers.
medications: ALK: Alectinib 600 mg BD or Lorlatinib
Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell).precautions: Immunotherapy → immune-related adverse events (pneumonitis, colitis, thyroiditis, hepatitis). Smoking cessation.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Small Cell Lung Cancer.name: Small Cell Lung Cancer
Small Cell Lung Cancer.symptoms: Rapidly progressing cough, dyspnea, weight loss, superior vena cava obstruction syndrome (facial/neck swelling, dilated neck veins), hyponatremia from SIADH, Cushingoid symptoms from ectopic ACTH
symptoms_list: superior vena cava obstruction syndrome (facial/neck swelling
Small Cell Lung Cancer.treatment: Limited stage: concurrent chemoradiation ± consolidation Durvalumab, prophylactic cranial irradiation/MRI surveillance. Extensive stage: chemo-immunotherapy.
Small Cell Lung Cancer.precautions: Watch tumour lysis, febrile neutropenia, paraneoplastic syndromes.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Small Cell Lung Cancer symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis.name: Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis
Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis.symptoms: Gradual progressive breathlessness on exertion, chronic dry cough, history of heavy exposure to silica dust in mining, quarrying, sandblasting, or stone cutting
symptoms_list: history of heavy exposure to silica dust in mining
Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis.treatment: Remove from exposure; no specific therapy; treat complications (TB, COPD, respiratory failure); lung transplant; oxygen.
Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis.precautions: Workplace dust control, respirators, regular screening of workers (mining, stone cutting, sandblasting).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.name: Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA)
Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.symptoms: Poorly controlled severe asthma with recurrent wheezing flares, coughing brownish-black mucus plugs, low-grade fever, malaise, peripheral blood eosinophilia, high IgE
symptoms_list: Poorly controlled severe asthma with recurrent wheezing flares
Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.treatment: Steroids to control inflammation, antifungals to reduce fungal burden; manage underlying asthma/CF.
medications: Prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg/day × 2–4 weeks then taper over 3–5 months
Itraconazole 200 mg BD × 16 weeks (alternative to steroids or adjunct)
Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.precautions: Itraconazole interactions (CYP3A4) and hepatotoxicity; monitor IgE for relapse.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Asperg.name: Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Aspergilloma
Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Asperg.symptoms: Recurrent hemoptysis (ranging from blood-streaked sputum to massive bleeding), chronic cough, weight loss, history of pre-existing tuberculous lung cavity
symptoms_list: Recurrent hemoptysis (ranging from blood-streaked sputum to massive bleeding)
history of pre-existing tuberculous lung cavity
Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Asperg.treatment: Asymptomatic simple aspergilloma → observation or surgery; chronic cavitary disease → long-term antifungal; hemoptysis → bronchial artery embolization or resection.
medications: Itraconazole 200 mg BD or Voriconazole 200 mg BD for ≥6 months
Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Asperg.precautions: Therapeutic drug monitoring for azoles; voriconazole → visual disturbances, photosensitivity, skin cancer.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Aspergilloma symptoms.

Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis.name: Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis
Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis.symptoms: Fever refractory to broad-spectrum antibiotics, pleuritic chest pain, hemoptysis, cough in severely immunocompromised or neutropenic patients, CT halo sign
symptoms_list: cough in severely immunocompromised or neutropenic patients
Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis.treatment: Urgent antifungal therapy in immunocompromised (neutropenia, transplant, high-dose steroids); reduce immunosuppression.
medications: Voriconazole 6 mg/kg IV q12h × 2 then 4 mg/kg q12h
Isavuconazole 200 mg q8h × 6 doses then OD
Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis.precautions: Voriconazole TDM (trough 1–5.5), many interactions (tacrolimus, cyclosporine). Amphotericin → nephrotoxicity, hypokalemia.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP).name: Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP)
Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP).symptoms: Insidious progressive exertional dyspnea, dry non-productive cough, fever, profound hypoxemia out of proportion to exam findings, bilateral interstitial infiltrates in HIV/CD4 < 200
symptoms_list: profound hypoxemia out of proportion to exam findings
Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP).treatment: Antimicrobial therapy 21 days; adjunct steroids if PaO₂ <70 mmHg (HIV); start ART within 2 weeks; secondary prophylaxis.
medications: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 15–20 mg/kg/day (TMP component) in 3–4 divided doses
Prednisone 40 mg BD × 5 days, 40 mg OD × 5 days, 20 mg OD × 11 days
alternatives: Primaquine + Clindamycin, Atovaquone. Prophylaxis: TMP-SMX 1 DS daily (CD4 <200).
Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP).precautions: TMP-SMX → hyperkalemia, rash/SJS, cytopenia. Check G6PD before primaquine/dapsone.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Bronchitis.symptoms: Cough lasting 1-3 weeks following viral upper respiratory infection, clear to purulent sputum, retrosternal burning or chest soreness, low-grade fever, no signs of pneumonia

Influenza.name: Influenza
Influenza.symptoms: Abrupt high fever, severe generalized body aches and myalgias, headache, dry cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, profound fatigue
investigations: Rapid influenza diagnostic test (RIDT) or RT-PCR if high-risk
Influenza.treatment: Strict bed rest, aggressive hydration, antipyretics (Paracetamol) for fever/myalgia, antiviral therapy (Oseltamivir) within 48h for high-risk patients.
Influenza.precautions: Isolate from high-risk family members (elderly, infants, pregnant women). Avoid Aspirin in children and adolescents due to Reye's syndrome risk. Seek immediate emergency care if breathing difficulty develops.
emergency_flags: Shortness of breath, rapid breathing, or oxygen saturation < 94%
Confusion, dizziness, or inability to wake up
Fever that improves then returns with a worse cough

Influenza.dosage_frequency: Paracetamol TDS (8 hourly SOS); Oseltamivir BD if prescribed by doctor
home_care_advice: Strict bed rest for first 3-5 days to allow immune recovery
Drink plenty of fluids: warm water, soups, ORS, herbal tea
Wear a mask around vulnerable household members
Use steam inhalation 2-3 times daily for airway comfort

COVID-19.name: COVID-19
COVID-19.symptoms: Fever, dry cough, profound fatigue, loss of taste (ageusia) or smell (anosmia), sore throat, headache, shortness of breath, body aches, gastrointestinal symptoms
COVID-19.treatment: Mild: symptomatic; high-risk mild: antivirals within 5 days; hospitalized hypoxic: oxygen, dexamethasone, anticoagulation prophylaxis, immunomodulators for progressive disease.
medications: Remdesivir 200 mg IV then 100 mg OD × 3–5 days
Dexamethasone 6 mg OD × 10 days (if requiring O₂)
Baricitinib or Tocilizumab for rapidly progressing
COVID-19.precautions: Ritonavir has major interactions (statins, anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, immunosuppressants) — check before prescribing. No steroids for non-hypoxic patients.

Pertussis (Whooping Cough).name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
Pertussis (Whooping Cough).symptoms: Catarrhal phase of mild cough and runny nose followed by paroxysms of violent coughing fits ending with a high-pitched inspiratory 'whoop', post-tussive vomiting, subconjunctival hemorrhages
symptoms_list: Catarrhal phase of mild cough and runny nose followed by paroxysms of violent coughing fits ending with a high-pitched inspiratory 'whoop'
Pertussis (Whooping Cough).treatment: Macrolide antibiotics (reduce transmission, shorten illness if early), supportive care, hospitalization for infants; prophylaxis for close contacts.
medications: Azithromycin 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2–5 (children 10 mg/kg day 1 then 5 mg/kg)
Pertussis (Whooping Cough).precautions: Infants <6 months at risk of apnea; erythromycin in neonates → pyloric stenosis (prefer azithromycin). Tdap in pregnancy (27–36 weeks).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Pertussis (Whooping Cough) symptoms.

Diphtheria.name: Diphtheria
Diphtheria.symptoms: Sore throat, low-grade fever, cervical lymphadenopathy ('bull neck' appearance), dense greyish-white pseudomembrane over tonsils and pharynx that bleeds when dislodged, stridor
symptoms_list: dense greyish-white pseudomembrane over tonsils and pharynx that bleeds when dislodged
Diphtheria.treatment: Hospital isolation, diphtheria antitoxin urgently, antibiotics, airway protection; cardiac monitoring.
medications: Diphtheria antitoxin 20,000–100,000 units IV (after sensitivity test)
Penicillin G or Erythromycin 500 mg QID × 14 days
Diphtheria.precautions: Notifiable disease; myocarditis and neuropathy may appear weeks later. Antitoxin anaphylaxis risk.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Diphtheria symptoms.

Hemoptysis (Massive).name: Hemoptysis (Massive)
Hemoptysis (Massive).symptoms: Expectorating large volumes of fresh bright red blood (> 100-200 mL in 24 hours), respiratory distress, choking sensation, hemodynamic instability
symptoms_list: Expectorating large volumes of fresh bright red blood (> 100-200 mL in 24 hours)
Hemoptysis (Massive).treatment: Airway protection, position bleeding side down, intubation with large tube/selective, bronchoscopy, bronchial artery embolization, surgery.
medications: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV TDS or nebulized 500 mg
correct coagulopathy (vitamin K, FFP, reversal agents)
Hemoptysis (Massive).precautions: Death is from asphyxiation, not exsanguination — airway first.

Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Commo.name: Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Common Cold)
Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Commo.symptoms: Nasal congestion, runny nose (rhinorrhea), sneezing, sore throat, mild dry cough, low-grade fever, malaise, head heaviness
investigations: CBC if symptoms persist beyond 7-10 days
Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Commo.treatment: Symptomatic relief, steam inhalation, warm saline gargles, adequate hydration, rest, and OTC antihistamine/decongestant combination.
Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Commo.precautions: May cause mild drowsiness; avoid driving or operating heavy machinery. Caution in patients with uncontrolled hypertension. Stay well hydrated. Do not take antibiotics for uncomplicated viral common cold.
emergency_flags: Severe shortness of breath, rapid breathing, or wheezing
High fever exceeding 102F that does not subside after 3 days
Inability to swallow liquids or severe earache

Peptic Ulcer Disease.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
Peptic Ulcer Disease.symptoms: Epigastric gnawing or burning pain occurring 2-3 hours after meals or at night, temporarily relieved by food or antacids (duodenal) or worsened by food (gastric), early satiety, nausea
symptoms_list: Epigastric gnawing or burning pain occurring 2-3 hours after meals or at night
temporarily relieved by food or antacids (duodenal) or worsened by food (gastric)
investigations: H. pylori testing (urea breath test, stool antigen, biopsy urease)
Peptic Ulcer Disease.treatment: PPI, eradicate H. pylori, stop NSAIDs; endoscopic therapy if bleeding.
medications: Omeprazole 20–40 mg OD (BD with H. pylori) for 4–8 weeks
Peptic Ulcer Disease.precautions: Stop PPI 2 weeks before H. pylori breath/stool test. Repeat endoscopy for gastric ulcers to confirm healing (exclude malignancy).

Helicobacter pylori Infection.name: Helicobacter pylori Infection
Helicobacter pylori Infection.symptoms: Persistent dyspepsia, epigastric discomfort, bloating, postprandial fullness, belching, nausea, history of recurrent gastritis or peptic ulcers
symptoms_list: history of recurrent gastritis or peptic ulcers
investigations: serology not for confirming active infection.
Helicobacter pylori Infection.treatment: Test-and-treat; confirm eradication ≥4 weeks after therapy. ACG 2024: optimized bismuth quadruple therapy 14 days first line; avoid empirical PPI-clarithromycin triple therapy unless clarithromycin susceptibility is confirmed.
medications: Bismuth quadruple: PPI BD + Bismuth subcitrate 120–300 mg or subsalicylate 262–524 mg QID + Tetracycline 500 mg QID + Metronidazole 500 mg TDS–QID × 14 days. Alternatives: Vonoprazan 20 mg BD + Amoxicillin 1 g TDS × 14 days
Helicobacter pylori Infection.precautions: Metronidazole + alcohol → disulfiram-like reaction. Tetracycline contraindicated in pregnancy/children <8. Bismuth darkens stool/tongue.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Helicobacter pylori Infection symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.name: Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding
Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.symptoms: Hematemesis (vomiting bright red blood or coffee-ground material), melena (black tarry sticky foul-smelling stools), orthostatic lightheadedness, syncope, tachycardia, hypotension
symptoms_list: Hematemesis (vomiting bright red blood or coffee-ground material)
investigations: CT angiography if endoscopy negative and active bleeding.
Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.treatment: Resuscitation (2 large-bore IV, restrictive transfusion Hb target 7–8 g/dL, 8 if cardiac disease), risk stratify (Glasgow-Blatchford), endoscopy within 24 h (within 12 h for variceal), endoscopic hemostasis; IR embolization or surgery if fails.
medications: Pantoprazole 80 mg IV bolus then 40 mg IV BD (or 8 mg/h) after endoscopic therapy for high-risk ulcers
Variceal: Terlipressin 2 mg IV q4h or Octreotide 50 mcg bolus then 50 mcg/h + Ceftriaxone 1 g OD prophylaxis
Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.precautions: Avoid tranexamic acid (HALT-IT — no benefit, more VTE). Manage anticoagulant reversal carefully.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding.name: Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding
Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding.symptoms: Hematochezia (passage of fresh bright red or maroon blood per rectum), lower abdominal cramping, tenesmus, dizziness, postural hypotension
symptoms_list: Hematochezia (passage of fresh bright red or maroon blood per rectum)
Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding.treatment: Resuscitation, colonoscopy after bowel prep (within 24 h), endoscopic hemostasis; CT angiography + embolization if unstable; surgery rarely.
medications: reversal agents (Vitamin K, PCC, Idarucizumab, Andexanet).
Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding.precautions: Hematochezia with shock may be upper GI source — consider OGD first.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Functional Dyspepsia.name: Functional Dyspepsia
Functional Dyspepsia.symptoms: Postprandial fullness, early satiety, epigastric pain or epigastric burning without evidence of structural disease on upper endoscopy, bloating, nausea
symptoms_list: epigastric pain or epigastric burning without evidence of structural disease on upper endoscopy
investigations: endoscopy if age >60 or alarm features.
Functional Dyspepsia.treatment: Reassurance, test and treat H. pylori, PPI trial, then TCA or prokinetic; dietary modification; psychological therapy.
medications: Itopride 50 mg TDS or Domperidone 10 mg TDS (short term)
Functional Dyspepsia.precautions: Domperidone → QT prolongation (max 30 mg/day, short course). Metoclopramide → tardive dyskinesia (≤12 weeks).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Functional Dyspepsia symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Gastroparesis.name: Gastroparesis
Gastroparesis.hindi_names: Pet ka dhere chalna; Delayed Gastric Emptying
Gastroparesis.symptoms: Nausea; Repeated vomiting of undigested food hours post meals; Early satiety; Epigastric fullness; Postprandial bloating; Epigastric pain; Weight loss; Uncontrolled blood sugar fluctuations
symptoms_list: Repeated vomiting of undigested food hours post meals

Achalasia Cardia.name: Achalasia Cardia
Achalasia Cardia.symptoms: Progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids, regurgitation of undigested bland food, retrosternal chest pain, nocturnal coughing, unintentional weight loss
symptoms_list: Progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids
Achalasia Cardia.treatment: Pneumatic dilation, laparoscopic Heller myotomy + fundoplication, or per-oral endoscopic myotomy (POEM); botulinum toxin for poor surgical candidates.
medications: Nifedipine 10–20 mg SL before meals or Isosorbide dinitrate 5 mg SL (limited efficacy)
Achalasia Cardia.precautions: Post-POEM reflux common — PPI surveillance. Increased risk of esophageal squamous cancer.
