Eosinophilic Esophagitis.name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis
Eosinophilic Esophagitis.symptoms: Intermittent difficulty swallowing solid foods (dysphagia), history of food impaction requiring emergency endoscopy, refractory heartburn, history of atopy or allergies
symptoms_list: history of food impaction requiring emergency endoscopy
Eosinophilic Esophagitis.treatment: PPI, swallowed topical steroids, elimination diets, dilation for strictures, biologic for refractory.
medications: Budesonide orodispersible 1 mg BD or Fluticasone 880 mcg BD swallowed
Eosinophilic Esophagitis.precautions: Food bolus impaction is an emergency. Oral thrush with topical steroids.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Eosinophilic Esophagitis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Esophageal Cancer.name: Esophageal Cancer
Esophageal Cancer.symptoms: Progressive difficulty swallowing (solids then liquids), painful swallowing (odynophagia), significant involuntary weight loss, regurgitation, persistent hoarseness
Esophageal Cancer.treatment: Early: endoscopic resection. Locally advanced: neoadjuvant chemoradiation (CROSS) or perioperative chemotherapy (FLOT for adenocarcinoma) + esophagectomy; adjuvant Nivolumab if residual disease. Metastatic: chemotherapy ± immunotherapy; stenting for dysphagia.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Esophageal Cancer symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Gastric Cancer.name: Gastric Cancer
Gastric Cancer.symptoms: Persistent unexplained dyspepsia in older adult, early satiety, epigastric pain, progressive weight loss, vomiting, iron deficiency anemia, palpable left supraclavicular node (Virchow node)
symptoms_list: Persistent unexplained dyspepsia in older adult
Gastric Cancer.treatment: Early: endoscopic submucosal dissection. Resectable: perioperative FLOT + gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy. Advanced: chemotherapy ± Nivolumab/Trastuzumab/Zolbetuximab (Claudin18.2).
Gastric Cancer.precautions: Post-gastrectomy B12 and iron supplementation; dumping syndrome advice.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Gastric Cancer symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Gastroenteritis.name: Acute Gastroenteritis
Acute Gastroenteritis.symptoms: Frequent watery or loose stools, abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, mild low-grade fever, malaise, dehydration
investigations: Clinical assessment of hydration and vital signs
Stool routine and microscopy if diarrhea persists > 48 hours
Acute Gastroenteritis.treatment: Aggressive oral rehydration therapy with WHO-formula ORS, oral zinc supplementation, probiotics, and light bland diet.
Acute Gastroenteritis.precautions: Do not take anti-motility drugs (like Loperamide) if there is fever or blood in stool. Avoid fruit juices, cow milk, and oily foods until gut recovers. Maintain strict hand washing.
emergency_flags: Signs of severe dehydration: sunken eyes, extreme dry mouth, dizziness on standing, no urination for > 8 hours
Blood in stool or black tarry stools
Inability to keep any fluids down due to persistent vomiting
High fever exceeding 102F or severe continuous abdominal pain

Fulminant: Vancomycin 500 mg PO/NG QID + Metronidazole 500 mg IV TDS ± rectal vancomycin

Pancreatic Cancer.treatment: Resectable: surgery (Whipple) + adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX. Borderline: neoadjuvant therapy. Metastatic: FOLFIRINOX/NALIRIFOX or Gemcitabine + nab-Paclitaxel; biliary stenting, celiac plexus block for pain.
Pancreatic Cancer.precautions: New-onset diabetes with weight loss in >50 years — consider pancreatic cancer. VTE risk high.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Pancreatic Cancer symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.

Acute Cholecystitis.name: Acute Cholecystitis
Acute Cholecystitis.symptoms: Severe constant right upper quadrant or epigastric pain lasting > 6 hours radiating to right scapula or shoulder, high fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, positive Murphy sign
symptoms_list: Persistent Right Upper Quadrant pain (>6 hours)
clarifying_questions: 1. Daahine taraf pet ke upar hisse me lagatar tez dard hai?
2. Chhune par tez dard aur saans rukti hai (Murphy sign)?
3. Bukhar hai?
investigations: USG Abdomen (thickened gallbladder wall >4mm, pericholecystic fluid)
Acute Cholecystitis.treatment: Hospital admission usually required; Low fat liquid diet initially; Complete rest; Do not apply local heat to abdomen
medications: Cefoperazone + Sulbactam (IV initial) then Cefixime OR Ciprofloxacin

Acute Cholecystitis.supportive_medicines: Hyoscine butylbromide 10 mg TDS SOS; IV fluids; Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy evaluation

Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Co.name: Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Colic
Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Co.symptoms: Episodic severe colicky right upper quadrant or epigastric pain occurring 30 minutes after fatty meals, lasting 1-5 hours, resolving completely, accompanied by nausea
symptoms_list: Episodic severe colicky right upper quadrant or epigastric pain occurring 30 minutes after fatty meals
Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Co.treatment: Asymptomatic → no treatment usually. Symptomatic → elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Low-fat diet.
medications: Diclofenac 75 mg IM or Ketorolac for colic
Ursodeoxycholic acid 10–15 mg/kg/day for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical candidates/after bariatric surgery.
Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Co.precautions: Porcelain gallbladder or polyp >10 mm → cholecystectomy (cancer risk).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Colic symptoms.

Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Cholangitis / Choledocholithiasis.name: Acute Cholangitis / Choledocholithiasis
Acute Cholangitis / Choledocholithiasis.symptoms: Charcot triad of fever with rigors, jaundice, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain; Reynolds pentad adds confusion and septic shock (medical emergency)
symptoms_list: Charcot triad of fever with rigors
and right upper quadrant abdominal pain
Reynolds pentad adds confusion and septic shock (medical emergency)
Acute Cholangitis / Choledocholithiasis.treatment: Antibiotics, fluids, biliary drainage by ERCP (urgent within 24 h if severe), then cholecystectomy.
medications: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h or Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole
Acute Cholangitis / Choledocholithiasis.precautions: Charcot triad/Reynolds pentad → emergency. Correct coagulopathy before ERCP.

Acute Viral Hepatitis A.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis A
Acute Viral Hepatitis A.symptoms: Abrupt onset of fatigue, malaise, anorexia, nausea, fever followed by dark tea-colored urine, pale stools, yellowish sclera (jaundice), tender hepatomegaly, history of contaminated food/water
symptoms_list: fever followed by dark tea-colored urine
Acute Viral Hepatitis A.treatment: Supportive; rest, hydration, avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic drugs; hospitalize if INR elevated/encephalopathy.
medications: post-exposure Hepatitis A vaccine within 2 weeks.
Acute Viral Hepatitis A.precautions: Fecal–oral spread; food handlers excluded until 1 week after jaundice onset. Watch for acute liver failure.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Acute Viral Hepatitis A symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hepatitis E.name: Hepatitis E
Hepatitis E.symptoms: Acute viral jaundice, malaise, anorexia, right upper quadrant discomfort; severe acute liver failure risk in pregnant women in third trimester
symptoms_list: severe acute liver failure risk in pregnant women in third trimester
Hepatitis E.treatment: Supportive; ribavirin for chronic HEV in immunosuppressed.
Hepatitis E.precautions: High mortality (up to 20–25%) in pregnant women (third trimester) — close monitoring. Ribavirin teratogenic.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hepatitis E symptoms.

Chronic Hepatitis B.hindi_names: Hepatitis B; Kalimati; Jigar ka infection
Chronic Hepatitis B.symptoms: Often asymptomatic chronic liver carrier; or episodic fatigue, right upper quadrant discomfort, jaundice, dark urine, spider nevi, palmar erythema in advanced cirrhosis
clarifying_questions: 1. Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) positive aaya hai?
2. Purani thakan ya peela-pan rehta hai?

Chronic Hepatitis C.symptoms: Insidious chronic fatigue, arthralgias, malaise, asymptomatic liver enzyme elevation; progressing over decades to cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and ascites

Alcohol-Related Hepatitis.name: Alcohol-Related Hepatitis
Alcohol-Related Hepatitis.symptoms: Rapid-onset jaundice, fever, anorexia, tender hepatomegaly, ascites, encephalopathy in a patient with heavy chronic alcohol consumption, AST:ALT ratio > 2
symptoms_list: encephalopathy in a patient with heavy chronic alcohol consumption
Alcohol-Related Hepatitis.treatment: Abstinence, nutrition (35–40 kcal/kg, 1.2–1.5 g/kg protein), thiamine, treat withdrawal and infection; steroids if Maddrey ≥32/MELD >20; early transplant in selected.
medications: Prednisolone 40 mg OD × 28 days (stop if Lille score >0.45 at day 7)
Alcohol-Related Hepatitis.precautions: Exclude infection and GI bleed before steroids. Avoid disulfiram and naltrexone in severe liver disease.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Alcohol-Related Hepatitis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatot.name: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD/NAFLD)
Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatot.symptoms: Usually asymptomatic silent liver fat accumulation; mild fatigue, dull right upper quadrant discomfort, associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia
symptoms_list: Usually asymptomatic silent liver fat accumulation
Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatot.treatment: Weight loss 7–10% (diet + exercise), manage diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension; avoid alcohol; MASH with fibrosis → pharmacotherapy; bariatric surgery for obesity.
medications: statins safe and indicated for CV risk.
Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatot.precautions: Cardiovascular disease is the main cause of death — address risk factors. Vitamin E long-term → possible prostate cancer/hemorrhagic stroke risk.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD/NAFLD) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Liver Cirrhosis.name: Liver Cirrhosis
Liver Cirrhosis.symptoms: Chronic fatigue, jaundice, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, gynecomastia, caput medusae, abdominal swelling (ascites), bilateral leg swelling, easy bruising, muscle wasting
investigations: etiology screen (HBV, HCV, ferritin, ceruloplasmin, autoimmune).
Liver Cirrhosis.treatment: Treat cause, abstinence, nutrition (late-evening snack), vaccination, varices screening, HCC surveillance, manage decompensation; transplant referral (MELD ≥15).
Liver Cirrhosis.precautions: Avoid NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, sedatives (benzodiazepines). Paracetamol ≤2 g/day. Avoid ACEi/ARB in ascites.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Liver Cirrhosis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacter.name: Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis
Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacter.symptoms: Progressive abdominal distension, fluid thrill, shifting dullness on percussion, rapid weight gain, shortness of breath from diaphragmatic splinting; fever and diffuse abdominal tenderness if SBP
symptoms_list: shortness of breath from diaphragmatic splinting
fever and diffuse abdominal tenderness if SBP
Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacter.treatment: Sodium restriction (<2 g/day = 5 g salt), diuretics, large-volume paracentesis with albumin, TIPS for refractory; SBP → antibiotics + albumin.
medications: Albumin 6–8 g per litre removed (>5 L paracentesis)
SBP: Cefotaxime 2 g IV q8h or Ceftriaxone 1–2 g OD × 5 days + Albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1, 1 g/kg day 3
Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacter.precautions: Stop diuretics if Na <125, creatinine rising, encephalopathy. Monitor for hepatorenal syndrome.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hepatic Encephalopathy.name: Hepatic Encephalopathy
Hepatic Encephalopathy.symptoms: Sleep-wake reversal, mild confusion, forgetfulness, irritability, asterixis ('flapping tremor' of outstretched hands), slurred speech, progression to stupor and coma
Hepatic Encephalopathy.treatment: Identify and correct precipitants (infection, GI bleed, constipation, hypokalemia, sedatives, dehydration); lactulose; rifaximin for recurrence prevention; nutrition (don't restrict protein).
medications: Lactulose 25 mL every 1–2 h until bowel movement then titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day
Hepatic Encephalopathy.precautions: Avoid benzodiazepines/opioids. Protect airway in grade 3–4.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hepatic Encephalopathy symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Esophageal Varices.name: Esophageal Varices
Esophageal Varices.symptoms: Asymptomatic until massive painless upper GI hemorrhage: vomiting large amounts of bright red blood, passing black tarry stools, lightheadedness, hypovolemic shock
symptoms_list: Asymptomatic until massive painless upper GI hemorrhage: vomiting large amounts of bright red blood
Esophageal Varices.treatment: Primary prophylaxis (non-selective beta-blocker or endoscopic band ligation); acute bleed → vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, EBL within 12 h, TIPS (pre-emptive in Child C); secondary prophylaxis NSBB + EBL.
Esophageal Varices.precautions: Avoid over-transfusion (raises portal pressure). Hold NSBB if refractory ascites with SBP ≤90 or AKI.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Esophageal Varices symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI).name: Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI)
Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI).symptoms: Rapidly worsening oliguria or anuria, rising serum creatinine, marked fluid retention in a cirrhotic patient with tense ascites and portal hypertension
symptoms_list: marked fluid retention in a cirrhotic patient with tense ascites and portal hypertension
Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI).treatment: Stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, volume expansion with albumin, vasoconstrictor therapy; liver transplantation definitive.
medications: Albumin 1 g/kg (max 100 g) for 2 days, then 20–40 g/day
Terlipressin 1 mg IV q4–6h (or 2 mg/day infusion) up to 12 mg/day
Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI).precautions: Terlipressin → ischemia, pulmonary edema/respiratory failure — avoid if SpO₂ <90%; monitor fluid status.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Acute Liver Failure.name: Acute Liver Failure
Acute Liver Failure.symptoms: Sudden rapid onset of deep jaundice, coagulopathy (INR >= 1.5), hepatic encephalopathy (altered mental status), sweet musty breath (fetor hepaticus) in a patient without pre-existing cirrhosis
symptoms_list: Sudden rapid onset of deep jaundice
sweet musty breath (fetor hepaticus) in a patient without pre-existing cirrhosis
Acute Liver Failure.treatment: ICU at transplant centre; identify cause (paracetamol, viral, DILI); NAC; manage cerebral edema, coagulopathy, infection, hypoglycemia; urgent transplant evaluation (King's College criteria).
medications: N-acetylcysteine IV 150 mg/kg over 1 h, 50 mg/kg over 4 h, 100 mg/kg over 16 h (also benefits non-paracetamol ALF in early stage)
Acute Liver Failure.precautions: Avoid sedatives; don't correct INR routinely (prognostic marker) unless bleeding/procedure.
emergency_flags: Acute liver failure with INR >= 1.5 and hepatic encephalopathy

Autoimmune Hepatitis.name: Autoimmune Hepatitis
Autoimmune Hepatitis.symptoms: Fluctuating jaundice, fatigue, arthralgias, amenorrhea, elevated serum IgG and transaminases in young or middle-aged women, often associated with other autoimmune diseases
symptoms_list: elevated serum IgG and transaminases in young or middle-aged women
often associated with other autoimmune diseases
Autoimmune Hepatitis.treatment: Immunosuppression to induce remission (normal ALT and IgG), maintenance ≥2–3 years; transplant for liver failure.
medications: Prednisolone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day tapered or Budesonide 9 mg/day (non-cirrhotic) + Azathioprine 1–2 mg/kg/day
Autoimmune Hepatitis.precautions: Bone protection; TPMT testing before azathioprine. Budesonide ineffective in cirrhosis (portosystemic shunting).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Autoimmune Hepatitis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Primary Biliary Cholangitis.name: Primary Biliary Cholangitis
Primary Biliary Cholangitis.symptoms: Severe chronic generalized pruritus (especially palms and soles, worse at night), progressive fatigue, dark skin pigmentation, xanthelasma, dry eyes and mouth in middle-aged women
symptoms_list: Severe chronic generalized pruritus (especially palms and soles
dry eyes and mouth in middle-aged women
Primary Biliary Cholangitis.treatment: Lifelong ursodeoxycholic acid; second-line for inadequate response; manage pruritus, osteoporosis, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency; transplant.
medications: Elafibranor 80 mg OD or Seladelpar 10 mg OD (second line)
Cholestyramine 4 g (4 h apart from UDCA) or Bezafibrate for pruritus.
Primary Biliary Cholangitis.precautions: Monitor ALP response at 12 months. Screen for thyroid disease, Sjögren's.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Primary Biliary Cholangitis symptoms.

Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.symptoms: Chronic fatigue, intermittent jaundice, severe pruritus, episodic right upper quadrant pain and fever from cholangitis, strong association with ulcerative colitis
symptoms_list: episodic right upper quadrant pain and fever from cholangitis
Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.treatment: No proven medical therapy; ERCP dilation of dominant strictures; manage cholangitis; surveillance for cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, colorectal cancer (with IBD); transplant.
Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.precautions: Annual colonoscopy if associated UC. High-dose UDCA harmful.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis symptoms.

Wilson Disease.name: Wilson Disease
Wilson Disease.symptoms: Tremors, dysarthria, dystonia, parkinsonian rigidity, psychiatric changes (personality changes, depression), golden-brown Kayser-Fleischer rings around corneas, jaundice, hepatomegaly
Wilson Disease.treatment: Lifelong copper chelation or zinc; low-copper diet (avoid shellfish, liver, nuts, chocolate initially); liver transplant for fulminant disease.
medications: D-Penicillamine 750–1500 mg/day in divided doses + Pyridoxine 25 mg
Wilson Disease.precautions: Penicillamine may worsen neurological symptoms initially; side effects (nephrotic syndrome, cytopenias, lupus-like). Screen siblings.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Wilson Disease symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hereditary Hemochromatosis.name: Hereditary Hemochromatosis
Hereditary Hemochromatosis.symptoms: Chronic fatigue, arthralgias (especially 2nd and 3rd MCP joints), bronze skin hyperpigmentation, diabetes ('bronze diabetes'), loss of libido, erectile dysfunction, hepatomegaly
Hereditary Hemochromatosis.treatment: Therapeutic phlebotomy (500 mL weekly) until ferritin 50–100 µg/L, then maintenance; chelation if phlebotomy not tolerated.
Hereditary Hemochromatosis.precautions: Avoid iron and vitamin C supplements, raw shellfish (Vibrio vulnificus). HCC surveillance if cirrhosis.

Hepatocellular Carcinoma.name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
Hepatocellular Carcinoma.symptoms: Unexplained weight loss, dull right upper quadrant pain, palpable hard liver mass, worsening of pre-existing cirrhosis ascites or jaundice, anorexia
symptoms_list: worsening of pre-existing cirrhosis ascites or jaundice
Hepatocellular Carcinoma.treatment: BCLC staging: resection, transplantation (Milan criteria), ablation for early; TACE intermediate; systemic therapy advanced.
Hepatocellular Carcinoma.precautions: Screen varices before bevacizumab (bleeding risk). Treat HBV with antivirals concurrently.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hepatocellular Carcinoma symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Colorectal Cancer.name: Colorectal Cancer
Colorectal Cancer.symptoms: Change in bowel habits (alternating diarrhea/constipation), unexplained iron deficiency anemia, hematochezia or melena, pencil-thin stools, tenesmus, weight loss in patients > 45
Colorectal Cancer.treatment: Colon: surgery ± adjuvant chemotherapy (stage III, high-risk II). Rectal: total neoadjuvant therapy + TME surgery or watch-and-wait. dMMR/MSI-H: immunotherapy (Dostarlimab for dMMR rectal). Metastatic: chemotherapy + biologics.
Colorectal Cancer.precautions: Screening from age 45 (FIT yearly or colonoscopy every 10 years). Oxaliplatin → neuropathy; Capecitabine → hand-foot syndrome; DPD deficiency testing before fluoropyrimidines.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Colorectal Cancer symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.

Diverticulitis.hindi_names: Aant me gubbare ki sujan; Diverticulitis
Diverticulitis.symptoms: Persistent Left Lower Quadrant abdominal pain; Fever; Sudden change in bowel habits (constipation/diarrhea); Nausea; Vomiting; Abdominal distension/tenderness; Dysuria (if bladder adjacent)

Hemorrhoids.name: Hemorrhoids
Hemorrhoids.symptoms: Painless bright red rectal bleeding coating stool or on toilet paper, prolapse of tissue through anus after defecation, perianal itching, or painful hard bluish perianal lump (thrombosed external)
symptoms_list: Painless bright red rectal bleeding coating stool or on toilet paper
prolapse of tissue through anus after defecation
or painful hard bluish perianal lump (thrombosed external)
Hemorrhoids.treatment: Fibre 25–35 g/day, fluids, avoid straining; office procedures (rubber band ligation) for grade I–III; hemorrhoidectomy for grade III–IV or thrombosed external (<72 h).
Hemorrhoids.precautions: Do not attribute rectal bleeding to hemorrhoids without excluding malignancy in at-risk patients. Prolonged steroid creams → skin atrophy.

Anal Fissure.name: Anal Fissure
Anal Fissure.hindi_names: Fissure; Latrine ki jagah katha hona; Katna
Anal Fissure.symptoms: Severe sharp tearing or burning pain during and for hours after defecation, streaks of bright red blood on toilet paper, extreme fear of passing stools, visible midline anal slit
symptoms_list: Severe sharp knife-like pain during and after defecation
Streak of bright red blood on stool/tissue

Stress Urinary Incontinence.name: Stress Urinary Incontinence
Stress Urinary Incontinence.symptoms: Involuntary loss of urine on effort or physical exertion, such as coughing, sneezing, laughing, lifting heavy objects, jumping, without premonitory urgency
symptoms_list: Involuntary loss of urine on effort or physical exertion
Stress Urinary Incontinence.treatment: Pelvic floor muscle training ≥3 months, weight loss; vaginal pessary; surgery (mid-urethral sling, colposuspension, bulking agents).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Stress Urinary Incontinence symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hyperkalemia.name: Hyperkalemia
Hyperkalemia.symptoms: Often asymptomatic until severe; generalized muscle weakness, flaccid paralysis, paresthesias, palpitations, cardiac arrhythmias, peaked T waves and widened QRS on ECG
symptoms_list: peaked T waves and widened QRS on ECG
investigations: ECG (peaked T, wide QRS, sine wave)
Hyperkalemia.treatment: ECG changes or K⁺ ≥6.5 = emergency: stabilize myocardium, shift K⁺ into cells, remove K⁺; dialysis if refractory/renal failure.
medications: Calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV over 5–10 min (repeat if ECG changes persist)
Insulin regular 10 U IV + Dextrose 25 g (monitor glucose)
Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g TDS or Patiromer 8.4 g OD
Hyperkalemia.precautions: Calcium does not lower K⁺ — it's membrane protection. Rebound after insulin/salbutamol wears off — recheck.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hyperkalemia symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
Hyponatremia.symptoms: Low Serum Sodium (<135 mEq/L; Severe <120 mEq/L); Mild: Nausea, headache, lethargy, gait unsteadiness, muscle cramps; Severe: Confusion, disorientation, seizures, cerebral edema, coma, respiratory arrest
symptoms_list: in acute severe drops (< 120 mmol/L) seizures
clarifying_questions: 1. Blood report me Sodium 135 se kam aaya hai?
2. Sujan ki dawai (diuretic) chal rahi hai?
3. Uljhan, chakkar ya ulti hui hai?
Hyponatremia.treatment: If SIADH/hypervolemic hyponatremia: restrict fluid intake to <800-1000 mL/day as advised; Do not drink excess water blindly; Take prescribed salt tablets
medications: Treat Underlying Cause + Fluid Restriction (if SIADH) OR Oral Salt Tablets / 3% Hypertonic Saline IV (if severe in ER)
Tolvaptan 15 mg OD (Vasopressin receptor antagonist for SIADH under specialist)
Hyponatremia.generic_drug: Treat Underlying Cause + Fluid Restriction (if SIADH) OR Oral Salt Tablets / 3% Hypertonic Saline IV (if severe in ER)

Hypokalemia.name: Hypokalemia
Hypokalemia.symptoms: Low Serum Potassium (<3.5 mEq/L; Severe <2.5 mEq/L); Generalized muscle weakness, leg cramps, fatigue, constipation; Paralytic ileus; Cardiac arrhythmias (flattened T waves, U waves, ST depression); Muscle fasciculations; Flaccid paralysis
symptoms_list: prominent U waves and flattened T waves on ECG
clarifying_questions: 1. Potassium report 3.5 se kam aayi hai?
2. Pairo me achanak kamzori ya kramps hue hain?
3. Dast, ulti ya paani ki dawai (diuretic) chal rahi hai?
investigations: ECG (U waves, ST depression, ventricular arrhythmias)
Hypokalemia.treatment: Take potassium syrup diluted in water/juice immediately after meals; Do not take on empty stomach; Avoid loop diuretics without potassium monitoring
medications: Potassium Chloride (Oral Syrup / Sustained Release Tablets) OR IV KCl (if severe in ICU)
Hypokalemia.generic_drug: Potassium Chloride (Oral Syrup / Sustained Release Tablets) OR IV KCl (if severe in ICU)
Hypokalemia.strength_mg: 15 to 30 mL (Potassium Chloride syrup - 20 mEq/15 mL)
Hypokalemia.dosage_frequency: BD or TDS (Diluted in a full glass of water)
Hypokalemia.supportive_medicines: Spironolactone / Amiloride (potassium-sparing diuretics); Magnesium supplementation (hypomagnesemia refractory hypokalemia)

medication_card.strength_mg: 15 to 30 mL (Potassium Chloride syrup - 20 mEq/15 mL)

Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.symptoms: Increased thirst (polydipsia), frequent urination especially at night (polyuria), increased hunger (polyphagia), unexplained fatigue, blurred vision, slow healing cuts
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.treatment: Lifestyle modification (low glycemic index diet, 30 mins daily walking), oral antidiabetic therapy (Metformin initial drug of choice), glucose self-monitoring.
medications: Metformin 500 mg with or after meals
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.precautions: Always take Metformin with or immediately after meals to prevent gastric upset or nausea. Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30). Monitor for hypoglycemia if combined with other secretagogues. Inspect feet daily.
emergency_flags: Hypoglycemia signs: trembling, profuse sweating, confusion, dizziness, hunger pangs (take sugar/juice immediately)
Very high sugar with persistent vomiting, deep rapid breathing, fruity breath (DKA / HHS risk)
Non-healing foot ulcer or blackening of toes
clarifying_questions: Kya raat me peshab ke liye baar-baar uthna padta hai?
Kya gala baar-baar sookh raha hai aur pyaas bohot lagti hai?
Kya chot ya zakhm dheere theek hote hain ya aankhon ke aage dhundhla dikhta hai?
home_care_advice: Reduce refined sugars, sweets, white rice, and refined flour (maida)
Walk briskly for at least 30 minutes 5 days a week
Monitor blood glucose regularly with a home glucometer
Inspect feet daily for cuts, blisters, or redness

medication_card.generic_drug: Metformin Hydrochloride
medication_card.precautions: Take with meals to avoid stomach upset; avoid in severe kidney failure; monitor blood sugar regularly.
home_care: Follow a low-carb, high-fiber diabetic diet
Walk briskly for 30 minutes daily
Check blood sugar regularly
Inspect feet daily for wounds

2. Pyaas aur bhookh zyada lagti hai?
3. Dhundhla dikhta hai ya zakhm dheere bharta hai?

Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.symptoms: Rapid onset of excessive thirst, frequent large-volume urination, nocturnal enuresis in children, rapid weight loss despite increased appetite, profound fatigue, blurred vision, diabetic ketoacidosis
symptoms_list: rapid weight loss despite increased appetite
Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.treatment: Lifelong insulin (basal-bolus or pump), carbohydrate counting, CGM, structured education, screening for complications and autoimmune diseases; Teplizumab to delay onset in stage 2.
medications: Insulin glargine/degludec/detemir (basal ~50% of total daily dose 0.4–1 U/kg/day) + rapid-acting aspart/lispro/glulisine with meals
Glucagon (nasal 3 mg or IM 1 mg) for severe hypoglycemia.
Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.precautions: Never stop basal insulin, even if not eating (sick-day rules — check ketones). Hypoglycemia awareness; driving rules (check glucose >90 mg/dL before driving).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Diabetic Ketoacidosis.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
Diabetic Ketoacidosis.symptoms: Nausea, intractable vomiting, severe diffuse abdominal pain, deep rapid sighing respirations (Kussmaul breathing), sweet fruity acetone breath odor, extreme dehydration, confusion, lethargy
Diabetic Ketoacidosis.treatment: Fluids, IV insulin, potassium replacement, treat precipitant (infection, missed insulin, MI); resolution: glucose <200 + 2 of (HCO₃ ≥15, pH >7.3, anion gap ≤12).
medications: 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid 1–1.5 L first hour
Regular insulin 0.1 U/kg/h fixed-rate infusion (only if K⁺ ≥3.5)
Potassium chloride 20–40 mmol/L of fluid if K⁺ <5.0
overlap SC basal insulin 1–2 h before stopping infusion.
Diabetic Ketoacidosis.precautions: Hypokalemia is the main killer — check K⁺ before insulin. Cerebral edema in children — avoid rapid fluid shifts. Check for SGLT2i euglycemic DKA.
emergency_flags: Diabetic ketoacidosis with severe metabolic acidosis

Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State.name: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State.symptoms: Extreme dehydration, profound lethargy, confusion, hallucinations, focal neurological deficits, blood glucose > 600 mg/dL, serum osmolality > 320 mOsm/kg, absence of significant ketoacidosis
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State.treatment: Careful fluid replacement (major deficit 8–12 L), low-dose insulin after fluids lower glucose, potassium, treat cause, VTE prophylaxis.
medications: 0.9% saline 1 L/h initially then guided by osmolality
Insulin 0.05 U/kg/h once glucose stops falling with fluids alone (or with ketonemia)
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State.precautions: Correct osmolality slowly (≤3–8 mOsm/kg/h) and sodium ≤10 mmol/L/24 h. High thrombosis risk.
emergency_flags: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state with glucose > 600 mg/dL

Hypoglycemia.name: Hypoglycemia
Hypoglycemia.symptoms: Sudden Blood Glucose <70 mg/dL: Tremors, Diaphoresis (cold sweat), Tachycardia, Anxiety, Hunger, Palpitations; Neuroglycopenic symptoms: Confusion, Dizziness, Slurred speech, Blurred vision, Seizures, Coma
clarifying_questions: 1. Blood Sugar 70 se kam aayi hai?
2. Pasiina, kapaahat, chakkar, aur bhookh achanak hui hai?
3. Insulin ya Sugar ki dawai chal rahi hai?
Hypoglycemia.treatment: Always carry glucose tablets, sugar pouches, or candy if on insulin/sulfonylureas; Educate family members on hypoglycemia recognition and handling; Re-evaluate diabetes drug doses with doctor
medications: 15 g Fast-Acting Sugar (First Aid) / Glucagon IM or 25% Dextrose IV (if unconscious in ER)
Follow with a complex carbohydrate snack (chapati/biscuit/milk) once sugar recovers >70 mg/dL

Hypoglycemia.strength_mg: 15 g Fast-Acting Glucose (e.g., 3 teaspoons sugar or glucose in water)
Hypoglycemia.supportive_medicines: Follow with a complex carbohydrate snack (chapati/biscuit/milk) once sugar recovers >70 mg/dL

Educate family members on hypoglycemia recognition and handling
Re-evaluate diabetes drug doses with doctor

Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome.name: Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome
Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome.symptoms: Usually asymptomatic; mild abdominal obesity, fasting blood glucose 100-125 mg/dL, HbA1c 5.7-6.4%, elevated triglycerides, low HDL, borderline blood pressure elevation
Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome.treatment: Intensive lifestyle (7% weight loss, 150 min/week activity — DPP trial: 58% risk reduction); treat BP/lipids; metformin in high-risk.
medications: Metformin 500–850 mg BD (BMI ≥35, age <60, prior GDM)
Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome.precautions: Annual glucose testing. Asian Indian cut-off for waist: ≥90 cm men, ≥80 cm women.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Obesity.name: Obesity
Obesity.symptoms: Excess body weight (BMI >= 30 kg/m2), increased waist circumference, shortness of breath on exertion, joint pain in knees and hips, daytime sleepiness from sleep apnea, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans
symptoms_list: joint pain in knees and hips
Obesity.treatment: Comprehensive lifestyle (calorie deficit 500–750 kcal/day, activity, behavior therapy); pharmacotherapy for BMI ≥30 (≥27 with comorbidity; Asian thresholds lower ≥25/23); metabolic/bariatric surgery for BMI ≥35 (≥27.5 Asian with T2DM).
Obesity.precautions: GLP-1/GIP agonists → GI effects, gallstones, pancreatitis, muscle loss (ensure protein/resistance training); contraindicated in pregnancy and MEN2/MTC history.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Obesity symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypothyroidism (Primary).name: Hypothyroidism (Primary)
Hypothyroidism (Primary).symptoms: Chronic fatigue, unexplained weight gain, cold intolerance, persistent constipation, dry rough skin, brittle coarse hair, periorbital puffiness, bradycardia, heavy menstrual bleeding, memory fog
investigations: repeat TSH 6–8 weeks after dose change.
Hypothyroidism (Primary).treatment: Levothyroxine replacement, titrate to TSH in reference range; subclinical (TSH 4.5–10) treat selectively (symptoms, pregnancy, antibodies, TSH >10).
medications: Levothyroxine 1.6 mcg/kg/day (start 25–50 mcg in elderly/cardiac disease) on empty stomach 30–60 min before breakfast
Hypothyroidism (Primary).precautions: Separate from iron, calcium, PPIs (4 h). Over-replacement → AF, osteoporosis. Rule out adrenal insufficiency before thyroxine in panhypopituitarism.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hypothyroidism (Primary) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Myxedema Coma.name: Myxedema Coma
Myxedema Coma.symptoms: Severe hypothermia, progressive lethargy, stupor, hypoventilation, bradycardia, periorbital edema, dry doughy skin, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia in untreated severe hypothyroidism
Myxedema Coma.treatment: ICU; IV thyroid hormone, steroids until adrenal insufficiency excluded, supportive ventilation, passive rewarming, treat hyponatremia/hypoglycemia and precipitant.
medications: Levothyroxine 200–400 mcg IV loading then 50–100 mcg IV daily (± Liothyronine 5–20 mcg IV)
Myxedema Coma.precautions: Lower doses in elderly/coronary disease (ischemia risk). Avoid sedatives.
emergency_flags: Myxedema coma with severe hypothermia, bradycardia, and hypoventilation
Immediate IV thyroid replacement and hydrocortisone

Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism.name: Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism
Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism.symptoms: Weight loss despite increased appetite, heat intolerance, profuse sweating, fine hand tremor, palpitations, anxiety, frequent bowel movements, bilateral exophthalmos (proptosis), diffuse goiter with bruit
Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism.treatment: Antithyroid drugs 12–18 months, radioactive iodine, or thyroidectomy; beta-blockers for symptoms; smoking cessation (eye disease).
medications: Carbimazole 20–40 mg/day or Methimazole 10–30 mg OD (titrate/block-replace)
Propylthiouracil 50–150 mg TDS in first trimester/thyroid storm
Teprotumumab for moderate-severe thyroid eye disease
Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism.precautions: Agranulocytosis (sore throat + fever → stop and check CBC). PTU → hepatotoxicity (avoid except 1st trimester/storm). Methimazole teratogenic early pregnancy. Radioiodine contraindicated in pregnancy/breastfeeding; may worsen eye disease (steroid cover).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Thyroid Storm.name: Thyroid Storm
Thyroid Storm.symptoms: Life-threatening thyrotoxic state: hyperpyrexia (fever > 40°C), severe tachycardia (heart rate > 140 bpm), atrial fibrillation, agitation, delirium, psychosis, vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, acute heart failure
Thyroid Storm.treatment: ICU; block synthesis, block release, beta-blockade, steroids, treat precipitant, supportive (cooling, fluids).
medications: PTU 500–1000 mg load then 250 mg q4h (or Methimazole 20 mg q4–6h)
1 h later Lugol's iodine 8–10 drops q6–8h or SSKI 5 drops q6h
Hydrocortisone 300 mg IV load then 100 mg q8h
Thyroid Storm.precautions: Give thionamide before iodine (avoid fuelling hormone synthesis). Avoid aspirin (displaces T4 from binding proteins).
emergency_flags: Thyroid storm with hyperpyrexia, severe tachycardia, and delirium
Immediate ICU admission and multimodality thyroid blockade

Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis.name: Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis
Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis.symptoms: Markedly painful and tender enlarged thyroid gland, neck pain radiating to jaw or ear, fever, malaise, transient symptoms of hyperthyroidism followed by transient hypothyroidism
symptoms_list: Markedly painful and tender enlarged thyroid gland
neck pain radiating to jaw or ear
transient symptoms of hyperthyroidism followed by transient hypothyroidism
Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis.treatment: Anti-inflammatory therapy, beta-blockers for thyrotoxic phase; temporary levothyroxine for hypothyroid phase if symptomatic.
medications: Prednisolone 40 mg/day tapered over 4–6 weeks if severe
Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis.precautions: Antithyroid drugs are ineffective (no excess synthesis).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid.name: Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid.symptoms: Painless solitary firm thyroid nodule detected by palpation or imaging, difficulty swallowing (dysphagia), hoarseness, anterior cervical lymphadenopathy
symptoms_list: Painless solitary firm thyroid nodule detected by palpation or imaging
Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid.treatment: Benign nodules — surveillance. Papillary/follicular cancer — lobectomy or total thyroidectomy ± radioactive iodine; TSH suppression as per risk; active surveillance for low-risk microcarcinoma.
Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid.precautions: Post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia and recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. Low-iodine diet before RAI.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid Cancer symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Primary Hyperparathyroidism.name: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
Primary Hyperparathyroidism.symptoms: Frequently asymptomatic hypercalcemia on routine blood tests; or classic 'stones, bones, abdominal groans, psychiatric overtones': kidney stones, bone pain, constipation, depression, fatigue
symptoms_list: Frequently asymptomatic hypercalcemia on routine blood tests
Primary Hyperparathyroidism.treatment: Parathyroidectomy if symptomatic or meets criteria (Ca >1 mg/dL above ULN, osteoporosis/vertebral fracture, eGFR <60, kidney stones/hypercalciuria, age <50); medical therapy otherwise.
Primary Hyperparathyroidism.precautions: Avoid thiazides, dehydration, lithium. Maintain normal calcium intake.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Primary Hyperparathyroidism symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy).name: Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy)
Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy).symptoms: Severe lethargy, confusion, dehydration, polyuria, polydipsia, severe constipation, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, shortened QT interval, cardiac arrhythmias in malignancy
Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy).treatment: Aggressive IV hydration, antiresorptive therapy, calcitonin for rapid effect, dialysis in renal failure; treat underlying malignancy.
medications: Zoledronic acid 4 mg IV over 15 min (renal-adjusted)
Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy).precautions: Bisphosphonates → osteonecrosis of jaw, nephrotoxicity, hypocalcemia (denosumab especially). Avoid thiazides.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy) symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism.name: Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism
Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism.symptoms: Numbness and tingling around mouth and fingertips (paresthesias), carpopedal spasms, painful muscle cramps, tetany, positive Chvostek and Trousseau signs, prolonged QT interval, seizures
symptoms_list: Numbness and tingling around mouth and fingertips (paresthesias)
Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism.treatment: Symptomatic/severe (Ca <7.5 mg/dL, tetany, seizure, QT prolonged): IV calcium; chronic: oral calcium + active vitamin D; correct magnesium.
medications: Calcium gluconate 10% 10–20 mL IV over 10 min then infusion
Calcium carbonate 1–2 g elemental/day in divided doses
Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism.precautions: Calcium gluconate preferred over chloride peripherally (extravasation necrosis). Avoid hypercalciuria (stones) — target low-normal calcium.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.
Shortness of breath, severe chest pain, or neurological deficits.

Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Ri.name: Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Rickets
Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Ri.symptoms: Diffuse bone pain and tenderness (especially lower back, pelvis, legs), proximal muscle weakness (waddling gait), difficulty rising from chairs, fractures; in children bowed legs, rachitic rosary
symptoms_list: Diffuse bone pain and tenderness (especially lower back
Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Ri.treatment: Vitamin D repletion + adequate calcium; sunlight; treat malabsorption.
medications: Cholecalciferol 60,000 IU weekly × 8 weeks then monthly (India common regimen) or 1,000–4,000 IU daily
children with rickets: 2,000 IU/day × 3 months or stoss therapy 100,000–300,000 IU.
Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Ri.precautions: Avoid mega-doses (>600,000 IU) — hypercalcemia. Monitor calcium in granulomatous disease.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation of Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Rickets symptoms.
Uncontrolled high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to take oral fluids.

Osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis

2. Usi taraf ki naak/aankh se paani aata hai?
3. Patient dard se bechain hokar tahlne lagta hai?
investigations: Brain MRI with contrast to rule out structural lesions
Cluster Headache.treatment: Avoid alcohol during cluster period; Maintain regular sleep schedule; Administer 100% Oxygen at 12 L/min via non-rebreather mask during attack
medications: Verapamil 240-480 mg daily (prophylaxis under specialist guidance)
Cluster Headache.supportive_medicines: Verapamil 240-480 mg daily (prophylaxis under specialist guidance)

supportive_medicines: Verapamil 240-480 mg daily (prophylaxis under specialist guidance)
medication_card.precautions: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Ischemic heart disease, coronary vasospasm, uncontrolled hypertension

Maintain regular sleep schedule

Trigeminal Neuralgia.name: Trigeminal Neuralgia
Trigeminal Neuralgia.hindi_names: Trigeminal Neuralgia; Chehre ki nass ka tez dard
Trigeminal Neuralgia.symptoms: Sudden, severe, electric shock-like, stabbing paroxysmal facial pain along V1, V2, or V3 distribution of trigeminal nerve (usually unilateral); Pain triggered by light touch, chewing, washing face, brushing teeth, smiling, or cold wind; Pain-free refractory periods between spasms
symptoms_list: Sudden recurrent paroxysms of severe electric shock-like lancinating unilateral facial pain along V2/V3 nerve branches
Trigeminal Neuralgia.typical_duration: Seconds to 2 minutes per spasm (recurrent episodes over weeks/months)
clarifying_questions: 1. Chehre par (gaal, jabde, ya aakh ke paas) achanak bijli ke jhatke jaisa tez stabbing dard hota hai?
2. Khana chabane, brush karne, ya chehre ko choone par dard shuru hota hai?
3. Dard kitni der rehta hai?
investigations: MRI Brain with thin-slice trigeminal nerve sequences (3D CISS/FIESTA - rules out neurovascular compression or Multiple Sclerosis)
Trigeminal Neuralgia.treatment: Avoid known facial trigger zones during acute flares; Wash face with lukewarm water using soft gentle dabs; Eat soft foods and chew on unaffected side; Avoid cold wind drafts directly on face
Trigeminal Neuralgia.dosage_frequency: BD initial, titrated slowly up to TDS by doctor
Trigeminal Neuralgia.supportive_medicines: Pregabalin 75 mg OD at bedtime; Baclofen 10 mg BD (under specialist supervision)

medication_card.generic_drug: Carbamazepine OR Oxcarbazepine
medication_card.dosage_frequency: BD initial, titrated slowly up to TDS by doctor
medication_card.precautions: Rx - neurologist supervision required. Carbamazepine is an antiepileptic drug; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN (risk of severe rebound pain and seizures). HLA-B*1502 genetic testing recommended prior to starting carbamazepine in patients of Asian/Indian origin due to risk of fatal Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Monitor Complete Blood Count (risk of aplastic anemia/leukopenia) and Serum Sodium (risk of hyponatremia). Causes drowsiness, dizziness, and ataxia
home_care: Avoid known facial trigger zones during acute flares
Wash face with lukewarm water using soft gentle dabs
Eat soft foods and chew on unaffected side
Avoid cold wind drafts directly on face
lab_tests: MRI Brain with thin-slice trigeminal nerve sequences (3D CISS/FIESTA - rules out neurovascular compression or Multiple Sclerosis)
emergency_red_flags: Severe generalized skin rash, fever, or mucosal ulcers (SJS/TEN reaction - STOP DRUG IMMEDIATELY AND GO TO ER)
Progressive facial numbness or motor weakness

Parkinson Disease.name: Parkinson Disease
Parkinson Disease.symptoms: Asymmetrical resting tremor (4-6 Hz pill-rolling), cogwheel muscle rigidity, bradykinesia (slowness of movement, small handwriting), postural instability, masked facies, festinating gait
Parkinson Disease.treatment: Dopaminergic replacement therapy, physical and occupational therapy, speech therapy, deep brain stimulation (DBS) for motor fluctuations
Parkinson Disease.precautions: Take levodopa 30-60 minutes before meals to avoid competition with dietary protein. Watch for impulse control disorders with dopamine agonists.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Parkinson Disease.

Alzheimer Disease.name: Alzheimer Disease
Alzheimer Disease.symptoms: Insidious progressive memory impairment (especially short-term recall), spatial disorientation, language difficulties (anomia), impaired executive function, behavioral changes, loss of independence
symptoms_list: Insidious progressive memory impairment (especially short-term recall)
Alzheimer Disease.treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors, NMDA receptor antagonist, structured cognitive stimulation, caregiver support and safety planning
Alzheimer Disease.precautions: Ensure home safety (fall prevention, stove locks, medication supervision). Avoid anticholinergic medications.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Alzheimer Disease.

Epilepsy (Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizu.name: Epilepsy (Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures)
Epilepsy (Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizu.symptoms: Sudden loss of consciousness, generalized tonic stiffening followed by bilateral clonic jerking, tongue biting, urinary incontinence, post-ictal confusion, headache, muscle soreness
symptoms_list: generalized tonic stiffening followed by bilateral clonic jerking
Epilepsy (Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizu.treatment: Anti-seizure medications tailored to seizure type, regular sleep schedule, avoidance of alcohol and sleep deprivation, driving restrictions
medications: Sodium valproate (avoid in women of childbearing potential)
Emergency buccal midazolam for prolonged seizures
Epilepsy (Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizu.precautions: Driving prohibited until seizure-free per statutory regulations. Never discontinue medications abruptly.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Epilepsy (Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures).

Bell Palsy.name: Bell Palsy
Bell Palsy.symptoms: Sudden acute onset of unilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness: inability to close eye, drooping mouth, loss of forehead wrinkling, hyperacusis, loss of taste on anterior two-thirds of tongue
symptoms_list: Sudden acute onset of unilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness: inability to close eye
loss of taste on anterior two-thirds of tongue
differential_diagnoses: Ischemic stroke (forehead spared in UMN lesion)
Bell Palsy.treatment: Early oral corticosteroids within 72 hours of onset, eye protection (lubricating drops and night taping) to prevent corneal ulceration
medications: Prednisolone 50-60 mg daily for 5-7 days then taper
Artificial tears eye drops hourly and lubricating ointment at night
Valacyclovir 1000 mg TDS in severe cases
Bell Palsy.precautions: Aggressive corneal protection is paramount until eye closure recovers completely.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Bell Palsy.

Multiple Sclerosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
Multiple Sclerosis.symptoms: Episodic neurological deficits separated in time and space: unilateral optic neuritis (pain with eye movement, loss of color vision), Lhermitte sign, transverse myelitis, sensory ataxia, spastic paraparesis, fatigue
symptoms_list: Episodic neurological deficits separated in time and space: unilateral optic neuritis (pain with eye movement
investigations: Brain and spinal cord MRI with gadolinium (periventricular/juxtacortical Dawson fingers)
Multiple Sclerosis.treatment: Acute relapse treatment with high-dose steroids; long-term disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) to prevent relapses and disability progression
medications: Methylprednisolone 1000 mg IV daily for 3-5 days for acute relapse
Multiple Sclerosis.precautions: Screen for JC virus antibody before natalizumab (PML risk). Maintain adequate vitamin D levels and avoid heat exposure (Uhthoff phenomenon).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Multiple Sclerosis.

Myasthenia Gravis.name: Myasthenia Gravis
Myasthenia Gravis.symptoms: Fluctuating fatigable skeletal muscle weakness worsening with repeated activity and improving with rest: bilateral ptosis, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, chewing weakness, proximal limb weakness
symptoms_list: Fluctuating fatigable skeletal muscle weakness worsening with repeated activity and improving with rest: bilateral ptosis
Myasthenia Gravis.treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors for symptom control, oral immunosuppression, thymectomy for thymoma or AChR+ generalized MG, IVIG/plasma exchange for crisis
medications: IVIG 2 g/kg over 2-5 days for myasthenic crisis
Myasthenia Gravis.precautions: Avoid drugs that worsen myasthenia: aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, beta-blockers, macrolides, magnesium. Monitor respiratory function (FVC).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Myasthenia Gravis.

Guillain-Barre Syndrome.name: Guillain-Barre Syndrome
Guillain-Barre Syndrome.symptoms: Rapidly progressive ascending symmetrical flaccid muscle weakness starting in lower extremities, absent deep tendon reflexes (areflexia), distal paresthesias, facial weakness, autonomic instability, preceded by viral illness or Campylobacter
symptoms_list: Rapidly progressive ascending symmetrical flaccid muscle weakness starting in lower extremities
preceded by viral illness or Campylobacter
investigations: Lumbar puncture (albuminocytologic dissociation: high protein with normal WBC)
Guillain-Barre Syndrome.treatment: Hospitalization and close ICU/airway monitoring, intravenous immunoglobulin or therapeutic plasma exchange; supportive physical therapy
Guillain-Barre Syndrome.precautions: Steroids are NOT beneficial in GBS. Monitor forced vital capacity (FVC) every 4-6 hours — intubate if FVC < 15-20 mL/kg.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Guillain-Barre Syndrome.

Generalized Anxiety Disorder.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
Generalized Anxiety Disorder.symptoms: Excessive, uncontrollable worry and apprehension lasting >= 6 months across multiple daily domains, motor restlessness, muscle tension, easy fatigability, concentration difficulties, insomnia
clarifying_questions: 1. Har chhotii baat par behadh chinta hoti hai?
2. Dil ki dhadkan tez hoti hai aur ghabraahat hoti hai?
3. Sone me pareshani hoti hai?
Generalized Anxiety Disorder.treatment: Practice deep breathing exercises (Pranayama); Limit caffeine and alcohol intake; Regular exercise; CBT
medications: Clonazepam 0.25 mg SOS (short term max 2 weeks)
Generalized Anxiety Disorder.supportive_medicines: Clonazepam 0.25 mg SOS (short term max 2 weeks); Cognitive Behavioral Therapy

medication_card.generic_drug: Escitalopram OR Sertraline
supportive_medicines: Clonazepam 0.25 mg SOS (short term max 2 weeks)
medication_card.precautions: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Suicidal ideation risk in young adults during first weeks; Do not abruptly discontinue (withdrawal syndrome); Serotonin syndrome risk
home_care: Practice deep breathing exercises (Pranayama)
Limit caffeine and alcohol intake
Regular exercise
CBT
emergency_red_flags: Active suicidal thoughts or self-harm intent
Severe panic attacks with chest pain

Panic Disorder.name: Panic Disorder
Panic Disorder.symptoms: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with sudden surges of intense fear reaching a peak within minutes: palpitations, diaphoresis, trembling, sensations of shortness of breath, chest pain, fear of dying or losing control, agoraphobia
symptoms_list: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with sudden surges of intense fear reaching a peak within minutes: palpitations
fear of dying or losing control
Panic Disorder.treatment: CBT with interoceptive exposure, breathing retraining, first-line SSRI/SNRI pharmacotherapy
medications: PRN Alprazolam or Clonazepam limited to acute crisis phase
Panic Disorder.precautions: Reassure patient regarding benign physical symptoms during panic attack. Avoid caffeine and stimulants.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Panic Disorder.

Bipolar Affective Disorder.name: Bipolar Affective Disorder
Bipolar Affective Disorder.symptoms: Alternating episodes of mania/hypomania (elevated grandiose mood, decreased need for sleep, rapid pressured speech, flight of ideas, impulsive risk-taking) and major depressive episodes
symptoms_list: Alternating episodes of mania/hypomania (elevated grandiose mood
impulsive risk-taking) and major depressive episodes
Bipolar Affective Disorder.treatment: Mood stabilizer pharmacotherapy, psychoeducation, structured sleep schedule, psychotherapy; avoid antidepressant monotherapy (risk of manic switch)
medications: Lithium carbonate 600-1200 mg daily (target serum level 0.6-0.8 mEq/L)
Bipolar Affective Disorder.precautions: Monitor lithium levels, renal function, and thyroid function every 3-6 months. Maintain consistent fluid and sodium intake on lithium.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Bipolar Affective Disorder.

Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.symptoms: PRESENCE OF OBSESSIONS (recurrent, intrusive, unwanted thoughts, urges, or images causing anxiety) AND/OR COMPULSIONS (repetitive behaviors performed to reduce anxiety); Common obsessions: contamination, doubt/harm, symmetry; Common compulsions: washing/handwashing, checking, counting, ordering; Significant time consumption (>1 hour/day)
symptoms_list: PRESENCE OF OBSESSIONS (recurrent, intrusive, unwanted thoughts, urges, or images causing anxiety) AND/OR COMPULSIONS (repetitive behaviors performed to reduce anxiety)
Common compulsions: washing/handwashing, checking, counting, ordering
clarifying_questions: 1. Dimaag me baar-baar unwanted khayal/darr (obsessions) aate hain jo rokne par bhi nahi rukte?
2. Unhe shaant karne ke liye baar-baar haath dhoona, check karna, ya ginte rehna (compulsions) padta hai?
3. Isme kitna time kharab hota hai?
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.treatment: Undergo cognitive behavioral therapy with Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) under a specialist; Practice resisting compulsions gradually ('delaying handwashing by 5 minutes'); Involve family to stop reassurance-seeking
medications: Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) Psychotherapy FIRST-LINE + High-dose SSRIs (Fluoxetine / Sertraline / Fluvoxamine / Clomipramine under Psychiatrist)
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.generic_drug: Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) Psychotherapy FIRST-LINE + High-dose SSRIs (Fluoxetine / Sertraline / Fluvoxamine / Clomipramine under Psychiatrist)
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.dosage_frequency: OD or divided BD under Psychiatrist
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.duration_days: Rx - psychiatrist supervision required (12 to 24 months)
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.supportive_medicines: Behavioral Therapy (ERP); Clomipramine (TCA second-line under specialist); Augmentation with low-dose Antipsychotics (Aripiprazole / Risperidone)
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.max_safe_limit_24h: 80 mg Fluoxetine / 200 mg Sertraline / 300 mg Fluvoxamine / 225 mg Clomipramine

Practice resisting compulsions gradually ('delaying handwashing by 5 minutes')

Ankylosing Spondylitis.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis
Ankylosing Spondylitis.symptoms: Inflammatory back pain in young adults (<45y): insidious onset, duration >3 months, MORNING STIFFNESS >30 MINS, IMPROVES WITH EXERCISE, WORSSENS WITH REST; Alternating buttock pain; Enthesitis (Achilles tendon/plantar fascia pain); Uveitis (red painful eye); Reduced chest expansion; Bamboo spine
symptoms_list: Inflammatory back pain in young adults (<45y): insidious onset, duration >3 months, MORNING STIFFNESS >30 MINS, IMPROVES WITH EXERCISE, WORSSENS WITH REST
clarifying_questions: 1. Umar 45 se kam hai aur kamar me subah uthte hi 30 min se zyada aedan rehti hai?
2. Kasrat karne par dard kam aur aaram karne par badhta hai?
3. HLA-B27 test hua hai?
investigations: MRI Sacroiliac Joints (detects early bone marrow edema/sacroiliitis)
Ankylosing Spondylitis.treatment: Perform daily lifelong posture, spinal extension, and deep breathing exercises; Sleep flat on a firm mattress with a thin pillow; Complete smoking cessation (smoking accelerates spinal fusion)
medications: Rx - specialist supervision required (First-line NSAIDs - Indomethacin / Etoricoxib
Sulfasalazine 500 mg BD (for peripheral joint involvement under rheumatologist)
Ankylosing Spondylitis.generic_drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (First-line NSAIDs - Indomethacin / Etoricoxib; Biologics - TNF/IL-17 Inhibitors under Rheumatologist)
Ankylosing Spondylitis.supportive_medicines: Sulfasalazine 500 mg BD (for peripheral joint involvement under rheumatologist); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Daily posture exercises

Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).symptoms: Multisystem autoimmune disorder: malar (butterfly) facial rash sparing nasolabial folds, discoid rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, non-erosive polyarthritis, pleuritis, pericarditis, lupus nephritis (proteinuria), cytopenias
symptoms_list: Multisystem autoimmune disorder: malar (butterfly) facial rash sparing nasolabial folds
investigations: Complements C3 and C4 (low in active flares)
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).treatment: Hydroxychloroquine for all patients unless contraindicated, photoprotection (broad-spectrum sunscreen), systemic corticosteroids for flares, immunosuppressants for organ disease
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).precautions: Strict UV sun avoidance with SPF 50+ sunscreen. Annual ophthalmological screening for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy after 5 years.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).

Sjogren Syndrome.name: Sjogren Syndrome
Sjogren Syndrome.symptoms: Chronic dry eyes (keratoconjunctivitis sicca, sandy gritty sensation), dry mouth (xerostomia, difficulty swallowing dry food), bilateral painless parotid gland enlargement, fatigue, arthralgias, increased dental caries
investigations: Schirmer test (tear production < 5 mm in 5 min)
Minor salivary gland lip biopsy (focal lymphocytic sialadenitis)
Sjogren Syndrome.treatment: Symptomatic eye and mouth lubrication, oral hygiene, cholinergic stimulation for secretory failure, systemic therapy for extraglandular manifestations
medications: Preservative-free artificial tears and ocular lubricating gels
Pilocarpine 5 mg TDS-QID or Cevimeline 30 mg TDS
Sjogren Syndrome.precautions: Rigorous dental hygiene and fluoride varnishes to prevent rampant dental decay. Monitor for lymphoma development (salivary gland enlargement).
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Sjogren Syndrome.

Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).name: Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma)
Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).symptoms: Skin tightening and thickening starting distally in fingers (sclerodactyly), severe Raynaud phenomenon with digital ischemic ulcers, telangiectasias, subcutaneous calcinosis, esophageal dysmotility, interstitial lung disease, renal crisis
symptoms_list: Skin tightening and thickening starting distally in fingers (sclerodactyly)
severe Raynaud phenomenon with digital ischemic ulcers
Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).treatment: Symptom-targeted therapy: vasodilator therapy for Raynaud, ACE inhibitors for scleroderma renal crisis, immunosuppression for active skin and interstitial lung disease
medications: Nifedipine 30-60 mg daily or Sildenafil for Raynaud
Mycophenolate mofetil 2-3 g daily for ILD
Prompt Captopril for Scleroderma Renal Crisis
Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).precautions: Never use high-dose corticosteroids (precipitates Scleroderma Renal Crisis). Monitor blood pressure weekly at home.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).

Psoriasis Vulgaris.name: Psoriasis Vulgaris
Psoriasis Vulgaris.symptoms: Sharply demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white micaceous scales on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees); Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding on scraping scale); Pruritus; Nail pitting; Psoriatic arthritis; Koebner phenomenon
symptoms_list: Well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered with thick silvery-white adherent scales
clarifying_questions: 1. Kohni ya ghutne par lal chakatte hain jinke upar safed chandi (silver) jaisi patti jamti hai?
2. Patti hatane par khoon ki boond dikhti hai?
investigations: Rheumatoid Factor & Anti-CCP (if joint pain present)
Psoriasis Vulgaris.treatment: Expose lesions to brief daily natural sunlight; Apply thick emollients daily after bath; Avoid skin injury/scratches; Avoid alcohol and smoking
medications: Clobetasol 0.05% + Salicylic Acid 3%/6% ointment OR Calcipatriol 0.005% ointment
Oral Methotrexate / Acitretin / Cyclosporine (strictly under dermatologist supervision)

Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema).name: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema)
Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema).symptoms: Intense severe pruritus, dry skin (xerosis), erythematous excoriated papules and plaques with lichenification, classic flexural distribution in older children/adults (antecubital and popliteal fossae), personal/family history of atopy
symptoms_list: Pruritic, erythematous, dry scaly papules and plaques with lichenification in flexural folds (elbows/knees)
clarifying_questions: 1. Bachpan se chamdi sookhi aur severe khujli waali hai?

Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.name: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.symptoms: Sudden onset of severe unilateral excruciating ocular pain, frontal headache, blurred vision, colored halos around lights, nausea, vomiting, cloudy steamy cornea, mid-dilated fixed non-reactive pupil, stony hard globe (IOP > 40-50 mmHg)
symptoms_list: Sudden onset of severe unilateral excruciating ocular pain
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.treatment: Emergency ophthalmological treatment to immediately lower IOP and clear cornea, followed by definitive bilateral laser peripheral iridotomy
medications: Acetazolamide 500 mg IV or PO stat
Topical Timolol 0.5% + Apraclonidine 1% + Pilocarpine 2% (after IOP drops)
IV Mannitol 20% (1-2 g/kg over 45 min) for refractory cases
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.precautions: Contraindication: NEVER dilate the pupil (mydriatics worsen pupillary block). Treat fellow eye prophylactically with laser iridotomy.

Acute Anterior Uveitis (Iritis).name: Acute Anterior Uveitis (Iritis)
Acute Anterior Uveitis (Iritis).symptoms: Unilateral aching deep eye pain, marked photophobia, eye redness with circumcorneal ciliary flush, blurred vision, constricted sluggish pupil, cells and flare in anterior chamber on slit lamp, association with HLA-B27
symptoms_list: eye redness with circumcorneal ciliary flush
cells and flare in anterior chamber on slit lamp
investigations: Slit-lamp examination (cells and flare in anterior chamber, keratic precipitates)
Acute Anterior Uveitis (Iritis).treatment: Urgent ophthalmological management: intensive topical corticosteroids and cycloplegic-mydriatic agents to relieve ciliary spasm and prevent posterior synechiae
medications: Prednisolone acetate 1% eye drops every 1-2 hours initially
Cyclopentolate 1% or Homatropine 5% eye drops BD-TDS to dilate pupil and break synechiae
Acute Anterior Uveitis (Iritis).precautions: Monitor intraocular pressure during steroid therapy (steroid-induced glaucoma). Complete course under ophthalmological supervision.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Acute Anterior Uveitis (Iritis).

Acute Otitis Externa.name: Acute Otitis Externa
Acute Otitis Externa.symptoms: Rapid onset of severe ear pain (otalgia) aggravated by tragal pressure or pinna traction, ear canal pruritus, feeling of fullness, purulent ear canal discharge, conductive hearing loss, edematous erythematous ear canal
symptoms_list: Rapid onset of severe ear pain (otalgia) aggravated by tragal pressure or pinna traction

Acute Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Poison.name: Acute Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Poisoning
Acute Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Poison.symptoms: Early phase (0-24h): nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis, malaise, or entirely asymptomatic; Day 2-3: rising transaminases, right upper quadrant pain, oliguria; Day 3-5: fulminant acute liver failure, jaundice, coagulopathy, encephalopathy
investigations: Serum paracetamol level plotted on Rumack-Matthew nomogram (at >= 4 hours post-ingestion)
AST, ALT, Bilirubin, INR/PT, Creatinine, Electrolytes, ABG/lactate
Acute Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Poison.treatment: Early activated charcoal if within 1-2 hours; IV or oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is life-saving and most effective within 8 hours; supportive liver failure care
medications: Intravenous N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) 3-bag protocol (150 mg/kg over 1h, 50 mg/kg over 4h, 100 mg/kg over 16h)
Acute Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Poison.precautions: Never delay NAC therapy while awaiting laboratory results if ingestion occurred >= 8 hours ago or dose > 150 mg/kg. Watch for anaphylactoid reactions to IV NAC.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Acute Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Poisoning.

Organophosphate Poisoning.name: Organophosphate Poisoning
Organophosphate Poisoning.symptoms: Severe cholinergic crisis (DUMBELS mnemonic): Diarrhea, Urination, Miosis (pinpoint pupils), Bronchorrhea, Bronchospasm, Bradycardia, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation; muscle fasciculations, weakness, seizures, coma
differential_diagnoses: Opioid overdose (pinpoint pupils but dry skin)

Organophosphate Poisoning.treatment: Decontamination (remove clothes, wash skin with soap and water), airway protection, atropine titrated until pulmonary secretions are dry, pralidoxime
medications: Atropine 2-5 mg IV every 5-10 minutes, doubling dose until bronchial secretions dry and heart rate > 80
Pralidoxime (2-PAM) 1-2 g IV over 30 min then 8-10 mg/kg/h infusion
Organophosphate Poisoning.precautions: Atropine reverses muscarinic effects only (not muscle weakness). Target endpoint is DRY LUNGS, not dilated pupils.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Organophosphate Poisoning.

Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.name: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.symptoms: Headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, confusion, fatigue, shortness of breath, visual disturbances, tachycardia, cherry-red skin color (rare, late sign), syncope, seizures, coma following indoor fire or faulty heating appliance
symptoms_list: coma following indoor fire or faulty heating appliance
Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.treatment: Immediate removal from exposure, 100% normobaric oxygen via tight-fitting non-rebreather mask; hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) for severe cases (COHb > 25%, pregnancy, syncope)
medications: 100% Oxygen therapy via non-rebreather mask until COHb < 3% and symptoms resolve
Hyperbaric oxygen (2.5-3.0 ATA) for severe poisoning

emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.

Opioid Toxicity (Overdose).name: Opioid Toxicity (Overdose)
Opioid Toxicity (Overdose).symptoms: Classic triad of coma / profound unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils (miosis), and severe respiratory depression (respiratory rate < 8-10 breaths/min or apnea); cyanosis, hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension

Opioid Toxicity (Overdose).precautions: Naloxone half-life (30-90 min) is much shorter than most opioids (especially methadone) — observe patient for >= 4-6 hours to prevent recurrence of apnea.
emergency_flags: Sudden severe exacerbation or complications related to Opioid Toxicity (Overdose).
